We show that this computational inefficiency is inherent, establishing a separation between the information-theoretic and polynomial-time regret achievable for this problem. Specifically, under the hypergraphic planted-clique conjecture, we show that for every polynomial-time algorithm there exist instances for which it incurs at least $(k\sqrt d)^{1-o(1)}$ regret.

papers.title: One Size Does Not Fit All: Curvature-Aware Adaptive Perturbation for SAM
papers.summary: Poor generalisation in deep neural networks is frequently associated with convergence to sharp minima. Sharpness-Aware Minimisation (SAM) improves generalisation of deep neural networks by minimising a combination of the training loss and the local sharpness of the loss landscape, biasing convergence towards flat minima. However, SAM relies on a fixed perturbation radius $ρ$ that ignores local curvature, leading to inefficient behaviour: the perturbation may be too small to escape poor basins defined by sharp local minima, or too large to allow convergence to solutions with good loss-sharpness tradeoff. We reinterpret $ρ$ as the intensity of the perturbation signal and propose Curvature-Aware Adaptive Perturbation for SAM (CAP-SAM), a geometry-aware method that modulates the perturbation radius based on a sharpness ratio, enabling a more effective search for robust minima on the loss landscape. We prove that CAP-SAM preserves the same convergence rate as standard SAM in non-convex stochastic settings. Extensive experiments indicate that our approach consistently outperforms SAM and its most prominent variants across diverse network architectures on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet.

papers.title: Hybrid supervised instance segmentation by learning label noise suppression
papers.summary: To reach top accuracy, current fully supervised instance segmentation methods severely rely on large-scale pixel-wise labeled datasets. They are usually expensive and time-consuming to obtain. Though weakly or semi-supervised methods utilize cheap bounding box labeled, image-level labeled or unlabeled samples to save the labeling cost, their performance is largely sacrificed. To save labeling cost without losing much performance, in this paper, we present a pipeline that can utilize economical bounding box labels and accurate pixel-wise labels in a hybrid way. Specifically, we design two ancillary models to learn label noise suppression and obtain accurate pseudo pixel-wise labels from bounding box labels for training. One is designed to suppress mislabeling between foreground and background, and the other is designed to suppress noise from mislabeling of instances. Moreover, we exploit category-aware spatial attention module, category constraint module, instance constraint module, and self-learning training approach to improve the accuracy of pseudo labels. Experiments on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and the Cityscapes datasets show that our method can achieve competitive performance with much less labeling cost.

papers.title: Compound p-values for competition-based testing
papers.summary: Standard competition-based multiple testing methods -- such as the knockoff filter and the target-decoy procedure -- are typically formulated as head-to-head competitions between a test unit and its assigned negative control unit. Motivated by real-world applications, which leverage any available negative controls, we study this competition-based framework in more intricate settings where competitions vary in size and structure. We propose new methods based on compound p-values -- p-values that are superuniform only on aggregate -- that enable powerful multiple testing with broader competition structures, via the Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg procedures. The former provides exact familywise error rate control, whereas the latter may incur a false discovery rate inflation factor, for which we derive upper bounds across a range of settings. We showcase the performance of our general competition-based testing methodology through extensive simulations and real-data applications, including analyses of virtual spatial transcriptomics and CRISPR screen datasets that exhibit precisely the complex competition structures that motivate our methods.

papers.title: Asymptotic behaviour for escaping an interval by Lévy flights under stochastic resetting
papers.summary: The resetting of stochastic processes has become a key mechanism appearing in many research fields, such as searching for a target, the transmission control protocol, biology, chemistry, finance, insurance, etc., with the main interest concerning the first passage time (FPT) by the process under resetting. In this paper, we focus on the exit time $\mathcal{T}_L$ from the interval $(-L, L)$ of Lévy flights (LF) under resetting, but we also consider spectrally negative Lévy processes (SNLP). As the main result, we find the asymptotics of the mean first passage time (MFPT) as $L$ tends to $+ \infty$. For LF with $α\in (0, 2)$, the scaling behaves as $L^α$ regardless of the reset rate and the asymmetry of the initial condition, a behaviour completely different from that for the known case of Brownian Motion ($α=2$). For the symmetric $α$-stable case with $α\in (0, 2)$, we also found that taking $r \to \infty$ with fixed $L$ yields a finite MFPT, which therefore may be used as a valid approximation. For completely asymmetric stable processes, we show that the scaling is very different from that for LF, and point out a method to obtain the exact distribution of FPT under resetting. The analytical calculations are verified by numerical simulations of the processes under resetting.

papers.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
papers.summary: Context can improve large language model performance, but these gains may be lost after context removal. Inspired by biological systems consolidation, we formulate Memory Consolidation (MC) as internalizing these gains while preserving non-target capabilities, connecting context-specified editing, skill learning, and behavioral steering under a common objective. We introduce a five-task-family testbed measuring consolidation and retention under single, batch, and sequential updates. We propose Cortex, which generates prospective queries to anticipate uses of context and distills context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural feed-forward network updates. Across 4B--120B dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, including both text-only and multimodal models, Cortex lies on the empirical consolidation--retention Pareto frontier in most evaluated settings. After 50 sequential factual edits on a 14B model, Cortex-Structural recovers 88.9% of the context-induced gain while retaining 99.8% of original non-target performance.

papers.title: Relative entropy in quantum field theory: the case of squeezed fermions
papers.summary: We review the role of relative entropy in quantum field theories, where the local von Neumann algebras are generically of type III. Consequently, only few exact results are known, and even bounds are difficult to obtain. As a new result, we prove that the relative entropy between a locally squeezed state and the Minkowski vacuum is finite for free fermions.
papers.comment: 34 pages, invited chapter for the book "Entropy, Relative Entropy, and Quantum Information Theory", edited by M. S. Moslehian, J. I. Fujii and Y. Seo, to be published by Springer

papers.title: Where Should the Gaussians Go? Reusable Label-Aware Allocation for Budget-Constrained Gaussian Splatting of Cinematic CT
papers.summary: Anatomical labels help 3D Gaussian splatting preserve vessels in cinematic renderings of CT, but the representation is still found by optimising each patient's scene, where densification decides where Gaussians go, while real-time displays cap their number. We address one part of this process: deciding where a fixed budget of B Gaussians should be placed. We propose a reusable, labelaware allocation front end that maps a patient's CT, labels and transfer function to a density over 2mm cells and draws exactly B positions from it without per-patient optimisation; the other Gaussian attributes are still fitted per patient. The front end is learned once from per-patient optimised scenes and implemented as a population-trained neural prior and an interpretable seven-parameter visibility-aware closed form (VACF). With identical attribute fitting on 20 held-out patients at 10K-100K Gaussians, both raise vessel-masked PSNR over uniform allocation by 4.5-7.1dB and over pruning a dense voxel-aligned model by 1.6-3.3dB. The neural prior does not differ significantly from per-patient optimised allocation at any budget, and VACF is within 0.6dB of it on vessels; on 19 external patients the neural prior again matches it on vessels and VACF is within 0.7dB. As an initialisation for position optimisation, VACF allocation beats per-patient densification on vessels at 10K Gaussians and, at 25K, reaches a higher vessel PSNR after 118s of optimisation than densification after 248s. Under altered rendering presets, VACF transfers to new colours and lighting but not to a label-free transfer function, whereas the neural prior shows the opposite pattern.

papers.title: Probing Planet Formation within 10 au: Dust Substructures in Extremely Compact Protoplanetary Disks
papers.summary: ALMA high-resolution surveys have so far focused mainly on large, bright protoplanetary disks, where substructures are routinely detected, leaving compact disks poorly characterized. Yet, the survival of millimeter emission in Class II sources implies that radial drift must have been halted by pressure traps, previously undetected due to limited angular resolution. We present ALMA Band 7 (0.9 mm) continuum observations of 11 of the smallest ($R_{68} < 10$ au) Class II disks in Lupus, reaching $0.02''$ (2 au) resolution, the highest currently available with ALMA at this wavelength. We detect substructures in 4 disks, including a clear inner cavity of radius 1.6 au, and hints of substructure in 3 more. Two disks also host faint outer rings beyond their bright inner core. Combining these results with demographic information on Class II disks observed with ALMA, we examine how the substructure detection rate varies with disk size, restricting to disks whose diameter is resolved by at least 3 resolution elements. We find that nearly all disks ($\gtrsim$95%) larger than 30 au show substructures, compared to a still substantial $\sim$50% between 3 and 30 au, with the lower rate likely affected by optical depth. The planet masses required to open gaps within 5 au fall in the super-Earth to mini-Neptune regime. These results demonstrate that substructures are ubiquitous across the disk population, and that planet formation conditions can be probed down to a few au from the host star.
papers.comment: Published in ApJL. 25 pages, 14 figures. Data products are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20559660

papers.title: FOLD: Position-Free Far Memory with Local Order for Long-Context Speculative Decoding
papers.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM generation through lightweight drafting and parallel verification. It is particularly promising for long inputs, where KV-cache access costs can be amortized over multiple accepted tokens. Yet most drafters are trained on short sequences and degrade on long inputs, while long-context training is costly. Existing training-free approaches restrict the context window, rescale positions, or augment recent context with retrieved distant entries. Drafters, however, read target hidden states that already encode contextual and positional information, and their lightweight architecture makes full-history attention affordable. We propose FOLD, a training-free method that preserves exact local positions and treats all distant entries as far memory at a shared position. To counter attention dilution as the memory grows, we sharpen attention within it to emphasize relevant entries while separately controlling its total weight relative to the local window. Across six target-drafter pairs and diverse benchmarks of up to 256K tokens, FOLD predominantly delivers the highest speedup, with the best case more than doubling the speedup over autoregressive decoding, from 2.08$\times$ to 4.22$\times$.

papers.title: STP-GUI: Spatially-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Web-GUI Agents
papers.summary: With the rapid development of vision-language models (VLMs), Web-GUI agents have achieved promising performance in interacting with real-world interfaces through screenshot-based grounding. However, high-resolution screenshots and multi-turn histories introduce excessive visual tokens, causing substantial inference overhead. Existing token pruning methods, mainly designed for natural images, often select tokens independently based on importance scores, which can fragment the local visual structures required for recognizing small GUI elements such as buttons, icons, and hyperlinks. In this work, we propose STP-GUI (Spatially-aware Token Pruning for GUI agents), a query-guided token pruning framework that preserves fine-grained instruction-conditioned token scoring while performing spatially coherent window-level selection under aggressive token reduction. A lightweight selector is optimized through policy learning while the VLM backbone remains frozen. Experiments on Online-Mind2Web show that \papername achieves a favorable efficiency-performance tradeoff under low token budgets. At 21% token retention, it preserves 77.7% of full-token performance while reducing inference latency by 31% and FLOPs by 57%. Results on Android in the Wild further suggest that the method transfers to mobile GUI environments.

papers.title: Modeling Diffuse Scattering in Mobility Scenarios: Ray Tracing Model and Measurement Validation
papers.summary: Open-source ray tracing (RT) frameworks are increasingly used for site-specific channel modeling due to their reproducibility and extensibility. In non-stationary mobility scenarios, repeated RT evaluations can generate different diffuse propagation paths without preserving their correspondence, limiting a consistent representation of their temporal evolution. To address this limitation, we extend diffuse scattering modeling in Sionna RT using persistent surface-associated scattering points. Their positions remain fixed, while their contributions evolve according to changes in the propagation geometry and visibility. The proposed approach is validated using empirical radio channel impulse response measurements in an urban vehicular scenario at 5.9 GHz. Compared with the standard Sionna RT baseline, the proposed model shows improved agreement with measurements in the delay and Doppler domains.

papers.title: Look Before You Restore: Learning to Predict Before Acting for Agentic Image Restoration
papers.summary: Agents for mixed-degradation image restoration typically learn what a tool does to an image only after running it: failed calls waste computation and harmful outputs go unnoticed until too late. We propose PreActIR, an agentic restoration framework that predicts tool consequences before execution. For each candidate tool, a tool-conditioned world model forecasts changes in residual degradation, image quality, and fidelity, together with the risk of harm and the uncertainty of the prediction. The agent executes the top-ranked candidate, and an independent verifier commits or rolls back its output before the agent replans from the observed state. PreActIR also audits whether performance is limited by the selector or by the candidate space, and studies targeted tool adaptation as a controlled way to expand that space. In a controlled evaluation that fixes the candidate pool, verifier, and budget and employs reference-annotated degradation states, PreActIR uses 42.5% fewer real tool calls and 63.4% fewer rejected calls than reactive, execute-then-evaluate trial and error, while improving Y-PSNR by 0.92 dB.

papers.title: Influence of the Néel vector on the bulk electronic structure of MnTe measured from the $(1 \bar1 00)$ surface
papers.summary: Altermagnetism gives rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization. Here, we use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to investigate bulk $α$-MnTe single crystals cleaved along the $(1\bar{1}00)$ plane - an orientation that preserves the compensated magnetic symmetry at the surface and substantially reduces surface effects and $k_z$ broadening. We resolve the three-dimensional bulk band structure with markedly enhanced spectral clarity. The $d$-wave band splitting, driven by the altermagnetic order and spin-orbit coupling in the $\mathbfΓ-\mathbf{K}-\mathbf{M}$ nodal plane, shows a perfect match to theoretical predictions. We further establish that the valence-band maximum occurs near the $\mathbf{A}$ point, identifying the corresponding hole pockets as the states governing the transport properties. Spatially resolved measurements reveal systematic variations of the band dispersion along $\mathbfΓ-\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{L}$, associated with different pinning of the Néel vector at the surface. Our results establish a surface-sensitive route to resolving the bulk altermagnetic electronic structure of MnTe and provide direct spectroscopic evidence for Néel-vector-dependent band splitting.

papers.title: Analog Cosmology in a Quenched Bose-Einstein Condensate Bubble
papers.summary: Recent interest and realization of ultracold bosons confined in shell-shaped, or bubble, traps have opened up several directions in the study of Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) in intrinsically curved geometries. Here, we explore the prospect of using thin spherical shell-shaped BECs as analog gravity simulators of an expanding or contracting curved universe. We study an interacting BEC bubble subject to a temporal quench of the interaction strength. Our theoretical approach, which uses a Bogoliubov treatment following a dimensional reduction of a spherical BEC to the low-energy excitations of a shell-shaped structure, demonstrates how this system serves as a laboratory analog for a positively curved universe having a time-varying scale factor. We investigate spontaneous pair production triggered by quenches associated with exponentially decaying or growing interaction strengths, focusing on the emergence of oscillations in the structure factor---analogous to Sakharov oscillations in the Cosmic Microwave Background angular power spectrum. We quantify the entanglement of the produced pairs via logarithmic negativity, and show how this measure may be extracted from the power spectrum. These findings establish a bridge between quantum information science and early-universe cosmology in a laboratory setting.

papers.title: Designing Hamiltonians with Exactly Flat Higher-Vortexable Bands
papers.summary: The zero modes of the Aharonov-Casher Hamiltonian form an exactly flat, vortexable Chern band in any nonuniform magnetic field, analogous to the lowest Landau level. We ask which local Hamiltonians host exactly flat higher-vortexable bands. For a scalar Hamiltonian, an exactly flat first-vortexable band requires a mass proportional to the local field; the Dirac analogue has the same structure. For periodic Bernal bilayer graphene with nonzero mean flux, the exact zero-mode pair is genuinely first-vortexable if and only if the interlayer hopping has nonzero mean; zero-mean hopping instead gives a decomposable pair. Multiorbital models yield exact higher-vortexable chains to arbitrary order, while remaining first order in momentum.

papers.title: Origin of the red spectral tilt in Inflation without an Inflaton
papers.summary: In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), a de Sitter (dS) background drives inflation, and the graviton bilinear generates scalar perturbations at second order, with no inflaton or additional fundamental scalar field. We investigate how this scenario can account for the observed scalar spectral tilt. The tensor-mode dependence of the scalar power spectrum gives the consistency relation $n_s-1=2n_T$, since it contains four tensor mode functions. The scalar spectral tilt $n_s\simeq0.9649$ at CMB scales therefore gives $n_T\simeq-0.0175$, independent of the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, hence different from the standard single-field slow-roll prediction $n_T=-r/8$. A full time-dependent calculation of $φ_2$ in exact dS leads to an almost scale-invariant scalar power spectrum, with a small blue infrared residual on the order of $n_s-1\simeq+4\times10^{-4}$. In order to account for the observed red tilt, we introduce a slow drift in the Hubble rate, parametrized by $\varepsilon=-\dot H/H^2$. The tensor tilt is then given by $n_T=-2\varepsilon$, implying $n_s-1\simeq-4\varepsilon$, at leading order. The observed tilt requires $\varepsilon_\ast\simeq0.0088$, far exceeding the drift that can be sustained by the classical graviton backreaction, for which we find $|\varepsilon_{\rm self}|\lesssim10^{-11}$. Therefore, we investigate the quantum break-time of dS as the origin of the background evolution. In this picture, the scalar tilt becomes $n_s-1=-4C_qN_{sp}(H/m_{pl})^2$, where $C_q$ is an order-one depletion coefficient, and the tilt is directly connected to the particle content of dS, $N_{sp}$. The evolution of the drift itself further predicts a positive running of $α_s=+\tfrac12(1-n_s)^2\simeq+6\times10^{-4}$. These results conclude the distinctive observational predictions of the IWI scenario, establishing it as a falsifiable alternative to standard inflaton-driven models.

papers.title: To Stack or Not to Stack? Jacobian Conditioning and the Benefits of Depth in Metasurface-Based Linear Transformation Synthesis
papers.summary: This paper investigates when and why stacking programmable metasurfaces into Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces (SIMs) improves linear transformation synthesis at a fixed phase-control budget. The analysis shows that algebraic Jacobian rank alone is insufficient to characterize practical synthesis, which also depends on the strength and balance of the sensitivity directions generated by the available controls. A layer-resolved analysis of the cascade model explains how inter-layer propagation can generate complementary sensitivity directions. The relevance of this mechanism is then assessed using an S-parameter multiport model that includes electromagnetic coupling and multiple scattering. Numerical results in near- and far-field sensing scenarios show that distributing the same control resources across multiple layers can strengthen weak transformation directions, improve Jacobian conditioning, and substantially enhance synthesis accuracy. These findings explain why increasing depth can offer benefits that are not obtained by simply enlarging a single programmable surface, and identify layer complementarity and Jacobian conditioning as useful criteria for SIM architecture design.

papers.title: Effective Graph Neural Representation of Chain Architectures of Block Copolymers Tested by Predicting RPA Instability Limits
papers.summary: Advances in polymer synthesis and computational modeling are expanding the block-copolymer architecture space accessible for phase-behavior design. Machine learning can accelerate this exploration, yet a common representation capable of learning across diverse chain topologies remains lacking. Here, we present a graph neural network (GNN) representation of acyclic AB multiblock architectures, tested by random-phase approximation (RPA) instability prediction. Each chain is represented as a graph, enabling a common model to learn across diverse topologies. This representation, which organizes RPA-related information, retains predictive capability when extrapolated to architectures with more blocks and demonstrates its potential for reuse across tasks through transfer to instability-wavenumber prediction. By effectively linking block-copolymer chain architecture to field-theoretic response, this graph representation not only reconstructs stability-limit curves but also provides a practical route for future self-consistent field theory exploration of ordered phase space across complex topologies.

papers.title: Component-wise outer similarity of turbulent boundary layers with strong adverse-pressure gradient
papers.summary: The adverse-pressure-gradient (APG) effect challenges the classical scaling of turbulent boundary layers (TBLs) over a flat plate, and it remains unclear whether outer-layer similarity holds across a wide range of APG strengths.We assemble a benchmark comprising the present direct numerical simulation of a suction--blowing-induced separation bubble and published profiles, spanning Clauser parameters $β_e=0.04$--$180$ and Reynolds numbers $Re_θ=530$--$19000$. Across this broad $(β_e,Re_θ)$ parameter range, existing APG normalizations do not simultaneously collapse the two mean-velocity defects and four Reynolds-stress components, leaving open whether outer similarity persists. Instead of defining new scalings, we normalize each quantity by its value at a common location $y_s$. Results are shown using $y_s=0.5δ$, beyond the outer stress peaks. For each of the six quantities, the normalized profiles exhibit a common outer shape across the conditions, with collapse emerging for $y/δ\gtrsim0.2$ for the velocity defects and $y/δ\gtrsim0.4$ for the Reynolds stresses. The collapse-error analysis shows that outer self-similarity is retained over a broad range of $y_s$ within the outer region and is not restricted to $y_s=0.5δ$. Furthermore, explicit expressions are provided for the normalized outer profiles. These results support component-wise outer similarity under strong APGs and provide compact references for APG turbulence-model assessment and conditional profile reconstruction.

papers.title: Continued fractions and passive ladder networks for acoustic impedances: the baffled piston and the horn
papers.summary: Lumped-element networks give transparent, passive models of acoustic impedances whose low- and high-frequency limits can be read from the circuit, but a systematic, arbitrarily accurate construction for non-rational impedances is lacking. Continued fractions, one- and two-point Padé approximants and their identity with ladder networks and Cauer synthesis are introduced in tutorial form and applied to two examples: the radiation impedance of a baffled circular piston and the throat impedance of a horn with a piston mouth. The even contraction of the piston's continued fraction has positive coefficients, certified by interval arithmetic for the first 100 pairs, and yields a ladder of positive resistances, masses and compliances; with 14 elements the error is 4e-4 up to ka = 5. Beranek's four-element network is, to about 2%, the order-two two-point Padé approximant. A horn modelled as a cascade of waveguide sections is a continued fraction whose tail is the mouth impedance; the infinite exponential horn is a periodic continued fraction, an exact high-pass ladder. The piston networks are passive at every certified order (up to 202 elements) and are extended without changing existing elements; for a finite horn the error of the mouth network passes one to one to the throat impedance.
papers.comment: 24 pages, 13 figures; to be submitted to Acta Acustica

papers.title: From Triage to Impact: A Multi-Hop Reasoning Benchmark for Explainable Persian Hate Speech
papers.summary: Hate speech has become increasingly prevalent on social media, raising concerns about its detection, interpretation, and moderation. Persian, a relatively low-resource language, lacks sufficient annotated data and computational resources for fine-grained hate speech analysis. In this study, we introduce a fine-grained, multi-hop benchmark for explainable Persian hate speech analysis, covering content triage, target identification, hate tactic and moral foundation analysis, textual evidence extraction, harmful narrative inference, and severity assessment. By evaluating state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs), we find that performance generally declines as tasks require more fine-grained semantic and inferential reasoning. Proprietary models generally outperform open-weight models, while reasoning-oriented models show no consistent advantage. Incorporating intermediate reasoning steps substantially improves severity prediction compared with one-shot assessment. Our analysis further reveals that Incitement to Violence or Harm is most strongly associated with higher severity, while political-affiliation targets are particularly associated with subversion-based moral framing. Overall, this work provides insights into LLM-based hate speech analysis and supports more accountable moderation of Persian-language social media. The benchmark is publicly available at https://github.com/kalhorghazal/From-Triage-to-Impact.

papers.title: Degeneracy graph determinants and higher-dimensional Young diagrams
papers.summary: Kemp and Ramgoolam proposed a basis of monomials for a commutative semisimple algebra with generators \(C_1,\ldots, C_L\), constructed from a degeneracy graph which records how the eigenspaces of \( C_1\) are successively split by \( C_2,\ldots, C_L\). They showed that the basis property is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the determinant of the matrix of values of these monomials on the projector basis, and conjectured a factorised formula for this determinant, as a product of powers of eigenvalue differences. We prove this formula for any number of generators. The proof uses graph analogues of Newton polynomials. Their evaluation matrix is not triangular in general, but expanding the rows of the children of each node of the penultimate layer in a Newton basis of their eigenvalues makes it block triangular, with diagonal blocks given by smaller degeneracy graphs in which the final layer is removed. The formula then follows by induction on the number of layers. We show that the exponents in the determinant are overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams attached to the nodes of the graph: intervals, ordinary Young diagrams, plane partitions and their higher analogues. Finally, the block triangular structure gives an explicit recursive inversion of the evaluation matrix, expressing the projectors in the monomial basis.

papers.title: Cascaded Retrieval with Cross-Modal Query Refinement for Efficient Visual Document Search
papers.summary: Retrieving information from visually rich documents requires matching queries against pages that contain complex evidence in tables, figures, and layout-dependent structures. Current vision-language retrievers address this but incur query-time costs that grow with corpus size and are impractical to scale. We propose SCOUT, a cascaded two-track retrieval framework that separates retrieval performance from exhaustive search. The visual track first uses a lightweight parent retriever to filter the corpus to a compact candidate pool, then applies a stronger multi-vector reranker only to those candidates. In parallel, a semantic track retrieves over hierarchical page and document summaries generated offline to provide a signal complementary to visual matching. The outputs are fused through cross-modal query refinement, which uses semantic scores to adjust the visual query representation before final ranking. We evaluate SCOUT on 4 major benchmarks against 6 baselines and observe a significant query-time latency improvement up to 80.7x (28.8x on average) relative to the best baseline, while exceeding state-of-the-art retrieval performance by up to 7.8% NDCG across all benchmarks.

papers.title: Regime Detection in Latent Factor Models -- A Bayesian Decision-Theoretic Approach
papers.summary: Regime-switching multi-factor models are widely used in quantitative finance, but filtering does not by itself determine when an agent should act on inferred regime changes. We formulate online regime detection with latent factors and hidden regimes as a Bayesian decision problem balancing false alarms, detection delay, and misclassification. Since posterior regime probabilities are generally non-Markovian, the problem is represented as a measure-valued optimal stopping problem and approximated using particle filtering with Monte Carlo dynamic programming. A single-change-point Heston model provides a benchmark. With observed variance, the problem reduces to a two-dimensional Markov free-boundary problem, while under latent variance decisions are based on the filtered posterior measure. Numerical experiments in Heston and regime-switching Vasicek models show that the latent-information procedure can outperform feasible plug-in rules.

papers.title: Lexical Persistence Without Semantic Entrenchment in AI Agent Communities
papers.summary: AI agent communities sustain lexical persistence, popular terms spread, recur, and achieve broad adoption, but whether they also develop the temporal semantic structure characteristic of human linguistic communities remains open. We compare MoltBook (AI agent community, 8 weeks), PTT (Chinese human BBS, 19 years), and Reddit (English human forum, in matched 8-week windows) using Compass-Aligned Distributional Embeddings (CADE), measuring semantic drift (B1), neighborhood stability (B2), and lag-1 autocorrelation of per-word drift trajectories. Across the platforms, lag-1 autocorrelation forms a memory-horizon continuum. AI agents' result clusters at the low end, while human platforms show longer-range temporal dependence. MoltBook exhibits approximately 2$\times$ the B1 drift and 20-30% lower B2 stability than both human platforms. As a partial control for community age, r/vibecoding (founded 2025-02-08) shows significant ACF in its first 8 weeks ($0.082$, $p<.001$) and over 15 weeks ($0.220$, $p<.001$); MoltBook's ACF remains non-significant ($p = 0.41$), consistent with the gap not reducing to developmental stage alone. We interpret this pattern as evidence that lexical diffusion alone does not guarantee diachronic semantic consolidation. The findings are consistent with a contrast between communities whose semantic trajectories accumulate long-range interaction constraints and communities whose outputs are repeatedly regenerated from largely fixed pretrained distributions.

papers.title: Excited-State Effects in Nucleon Sigma Terms from a Variational Analysis
papers.summary: We investigate excited-state effects in nucleon sigma-terms in lattice QCD using twisted-mass clover-improved fermion ensembles. We study correlation functions with nucleon and multihadron nucleon-$σ$-meson interpolating operators. The analysis is performed using three gauge ensembles, including one ensemble simulated with two degenerate light, a strange, and a charm quark with quark masses tuned to approximately their physical value. We solve the generalized eigenvalue problem that arises from the matrix of correlators and show that the three-point function for the light sigma-term obtained using the optimal linear combination of interpolating operators has substantially reduced time dependence without loss of statistical precision. We apply Laplace filtering and investigate residual excited-state contributions in the extraction of $σ_{πN}$. Using the same optimal linear combination of correlators as for $σ_{πN}$ for the strange sigma-term we also observe suppressed excited state contributions over an extended range of source--sink time separations. For the charm sigma-term, we observe negligible time dependence within the large statistical uncertainties, and these improvements show no significant effect.

papers.title: Modeling electrodeposition of thin films with compact, dendritic, and random morphologies
papers.summary: We summarize previously published computer simulation studies of a metal electrodeposition model that considers diffusive cation flux, a fast reaction in contact with the electrode or with the growing deposit, and adsorbed atom diffusion in finite time windows. Simulations with various parameters show compact, fractal, dendritic deposits, and dynamic transitions between different morphologies during the growth of individual samples. The dendritic shapes are characterized by hierarchical organizations in which branches of a given order reproduce the shape and crystalline orientation of the branches of the previous order, in contrast to the random branching of the fractal deposits formed by DLA and related models. The simulations show dendrites with maple leaf shape in SC lattices, pine tree shape in FCC lattices, and flower-like shape in HCP lattices, with surfaces predominantly oriented in the lowest-energy configurations of each lattice. Simulations with nucleation restricted to a nanoscale seed show the initial formation of faceted particles followed by dendrite formation, in agreement with silver electrodeposition on substrates patterned with gold nanoparticles. A quantitative application to faceted and dendritic silver obtained in the same experiment provides values of the model parameters which are consistent with the characteristic widths of these structures being of the same order of magnitude of the diffusion lengths of atoms on (111) and (001) surfaces. Using an extended model for iron electrodeposition on Si(100), the simulations qualitatively reproduce the initial formation of multilayer islands, small oscillations of the roughness of a polycrystalline compact film after island coalescence, and instability development. Possible directions for applying this modeling to the electrodeposition of other materials are suggested.

papers.title: Do AI Agents Gossip? Evaluative Talk in Human and AI-Agent Online Communities
papers.summary: Gossip, defined as evaluative talk about absent third parties, is widely seen as a uniquely human social practice. This study examines whether comparable discourse emerges spontaneously in a community of autonomous AI agents. We compare Moltbook, a Reddit-style platform populated by AI agents, with PTT, a large human-operated bulletin board in Taiwan. To reduce differences attributable to communicative setting, we analyze two public, asynchronous forums using the same operational definition of gossip. Gossip occurs on Moltbook, but its prevalence is 2.6 to 6 times lower than on PTT, depending on the denominator used. On both platforms, gossip frequently targets locally prominent figures, tends to elicit agreement from the first respondent, and is rarely presented as unsupported rumor. The clearest difference concerns how subsequent responses develop. Among threads containing at least one codable reply, challenges occur in 65.1% of human threads but only 21.3% of agent threads. Moreover, following an early aligning response, consensus remains unchallenged in 83.6% of agent threads, compared with 44.7% of human threads. This thread-level contrast remains after controlling for thread depth and board composition and under recalibration against two human annotators. Estimates based on individual reply turns are less robust and are therefore reported as bounds. These findings suggest that AI-agent communities reproduce the informational dimension of gossip, while the extent to which gossip performs comparable relational functions remains unresolved.

papers.title: Bouncing Bianchi Type I Universes with Interacting Vacuum
papers.summary: We investigate the global dynamics and cosmological viability of non-singular solutions in an anisotropic Bianchi type I universe featuring an interacting vacuum energy component $V$ and a perfect fluid $ρ$, extending previous work based on a Robertson-Walker geometry. By modeling the energy-momentum transfer via a phenomenological four-vector $Q_μ$, we reduce the field equations to a four-dimensional autonomous dynamical system for the expansion rate $Θ$, total shear $σ$, energy density $ρ$, and vacuum component $V$. We examine two distinct forms for how the interaction depends on $ρ$ and $V$: a linear coupling $Q_1 \propto Θ[ξ(V_Λ- V) + χρ]$ and a non-linear coupling $Q_2 \propto Θρ(1 - V/V_Λ)$. Using a potential-energy analogy and phase-space analysis, we show that the linear model $Q_1$ naturally admits non-singular bouncing trajectories. In contrast, unlike the Robertson-Walker case, for the non-linear interaction $Q_2$, invariant boundary surfaces in phase space strictly constrain the domain of expansion ruling out cosmological bounce scenarios for physical matter configurations.

papers.title: ReferFlow: Beyond Final-Target Localization for Complex Referring Expressions
papers.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models have made significant progress in referring expression comprehension (REC), yet most REC benchmarks still focus on final-target localization. Complex queries often involve intermediate visual references with different dependencies on prior grounding, but final-only evaluation leaves this process unexamined. To address this gap, we formulate trajectory-level REC, in which models receive an ordered sequence of grounding steps constructed from a single complex query and localize the target regions associated with each step. We instantiate this setting in ReferFlow-Bench, which characterizes structured region transitions through four trajectory types, namely Refinement, Shift, Reset, and Mixture. Experiments show that current models struggle to consistently ground intermediate visual references across successive steps. We further propose ReferFlow, which decouples interleaved text-latent trajectory generation from coordinate decoding. Specifically, Stateful Region Latent Reasoning represents each target region as an object-indexed state composed of continuous latents, with explicit visual and spatial supervision to preserve region information for subsequent grounding. Trajectory-Aware Parallel Decoding then recovers all coordinate blocks in parallel through four geometry-constrained refinement rounds, with each block conditioned on its corresponding trajectory prefix, thereby reducing within-box sequential dependencies and eliminating cross-box autoregression. We further apply Grounding-Aware GRPO to promote consistent grounding across steps and learn adaptive trajectory generation from complex REC queries. ReferFlow achieves leading performance on general REC benchmarks and ReferFlow-Bench.

papers.title: Human Demonstrations as Post-Training Data for Any Robot Body: Retargeting the Object, Not the Hand
papers.summary: Human demonstrations are today used largely for pretraining vision-language-action models, with little ability to use the same data for target-embodiment or task-oriented training, which scalable deployment of robots in industrial and general environments depends on. A human demonstration recorded on a simple and scalable device such as a mobile phone can serve as post-training data for a robot whose body differs in structure and capability from the human who recorded it. This is made possible not by retargeting the hand's motion but the object's. A capture yields a body-free record: the object's pose over time, its contact intervals, and a reconstructed 3D object with provenance. Any robot, given as a URDF and a short descriptor, is solved against that record and scored in simulation against the demonstrated object motion as ground truth: the human-to-simulation leg of human-to-simulation-to-robot transfer, measured per robot. Each (robot, episode) pair gets one outcome: pass, failure with a named mode, or refusal, with its reason, before any motion. The method runs as a working system over a growing collection; the set analysed here is a sample of it: 42 captures solved on 8 robots, 157 pairs, of which 31.2% pass, 52.2% fail, 14.0% are refused and 2.5% are unauditable (kinematic feasibility, +/-50 mm / +/-15 deg, in simulation). Refusals held up: every pair the checks refuse on stored evidence yet ran anyway failed (13 of 13; 5 on a body whose public model welds its hand). A description file could not be shown to screen a robot: its outcomes were barely more predictable than guessing. No policy has yet been trained on the record. The record decides what a robot may post-train on; whether the policy then works on the real robot is the simulation-to-robot question, answered downstream.
papers.comment: 16 pages, 17 figures, 7 tables, 2 algorithms; 56-page supplement as ancillary file. A subset of episodes with their per-robot outcomes: https://playground.dxtr.co

papers.title: Thermal properties of the $ρ$ meson from a machine-learning-improved holographic QCD model
papers.summary: The thermal properties of the \(ρ\) meson are revisited within the soft-wall AdS/QCD framework. The dilaton background is calibrated against lattice QCD screening-mass data through a neural-network-assisted inverse procedure. Using this calibrated background, we compute the temporal vector spectral function and the lowest vector quasi-normal modes. The pole mass \(m_{\mathrm{pole}}(T)\) and thermal width \(Γ(T)\) are then extracted from the corresponding complex quasi-normal mode frequencies. Adopting the vanishing real part of the quasi-normal mode frequency, \(ω_{\mathrm{Re}}(T_d)=0\), as a criterion for meson dissociation, we estimate \(T_d\approx168\,\mathrm{MeV}\). As the temperature increases, the thermal width grows, and the spectral function evolves from a narrow Breit-Wigner-like resonance peak into a transport peak, confirming the QNM prediction that the vanishing of the pole mass is accompanied by the emergence of a transport peak and making it difficult to identify a quasiparticle peak. A numerical extraction of the dispersion relation shows that the propagator can be described by a finite-temperature simple-pole form with momentum-dependent thermal width, characterized by a diffusion coefficient \(D(T)\) and an effective propagation speed \(u(T)\), whose temperature dependences are also extracted. This form modifies the usual relation between the screening and pole masses. These results may provide a useful reference for effective studies of the hot hadronic medium.

papers.title: Cavity-tunable Pseudospin-Hall Topology and Edge Transport
papers.summary: Topological edge states are a hallmark of topological phases, with their existence tied to bulk band topology through bulk-edge correspondence. In photonic pseudospin-Hall systems, these states exhibit pseudospin-momentum locking, with lattice interactions and interface geometry determining each pseudospin's propagation direction. Reversing the pseudospin-dependent propagation direction without altering the lattice configuration or excitation handedness remains a fundamental challenge in controlling topological edge transport. Here, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate cavity-tunable topological edge transport in a microwave metasurface embedded within a metallic cavity. Varying the cavity height reshapes resonator interactions, driving band inversion and topological phase transition while preserving the lattice geometry. For a fixed domain-wall configuration, this transition reverses the propagation direction associated with each pseudospin while preserving pseudospin-momentum locking. Excitations with the same handedness are observed to launch edge waves propagating in opposite directions at their respective edge-band frequencies determined by the cavity height. These results establish cavity electrodynamics as an external means of controlling the bulk topology and reconfiguring the directional response of topological interfaces, creating new opportunities for topological wave routing in fixed photonic lattice structures.

papers.title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views
papers.summary: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction builds 3D scenes directly from input images for novel view rendering, but learning Gaussian attributes from predicted geometry for high-quality rendering under large viewpoint changes remains challenging. We analyze limitations in Gaussian attribute learning and introduce InfiniSplat v2, which improves rendering quality through architectural and training changes. Our method decouples geometry and attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch, aligns predicted Gaussians using ground-truth camera poses during training, and adopts large-angle target view supervision. Across six datasets, the feed-forward outputs of the same trained model achieve state-of-the-art mean LPIPS and DISTS among the evaluated methods in both pose-conditioned and pose-free settings. In the pose-conditioned setting, mean LPIPS and DISTS decrease by 25.8% and 32.9%, respectively, compared with the strongest evaluated baselines. We further find that opacity learned with only image reconstruction supervision suppresses geometrically inconsistent points. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat2/

papers.title: Black hole cohomologies in N=4 SYM
papers.summary: We systematically investigate BPS cohomologies of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory with gauge group SU$(N)$ with $N=2, 3, 4$, focusing primarily on the BMN sector. We find non-Coulomb graviton cohomologies for $N>2$. For $N>2$, the lightest black hole cohomology in the BMN sector always carries non-trivial $R$-charge and corresponds to the brane-fused type. Therefore, the `core' black holes without hair are `heavier'. We also find that a family of brane-fused cohomologies in $N=3$ is not lifted at the first quantum order. At a fixed charge sector, gravitons carry definite parity under charge conjugation. Up to the levels we have tested, every black hole cohomology either has opposite parity to that of gravitons or is lifted by quantum corrections. We conjecture that black hole cohomologies always carry parity opposite to gravitons in the same charge sector.

papers.title: Dual-Polarized Rate-Splitting Multiple Access for mmWave Communications: A Practical Design and Prototype Implementation
papers.summary: This work presents a dual-polarized rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) design for millimeter-wave (mmWave) or frequency range 2 (FR2) communications. Focusing on a practical implementation, we consider the specific scenario of a single transmitter serving two receivers (users) within the same time, frequency, and code resource block. The transmitter and each receiver are equipped with a pair of dual-polarized antennas. We first present the system formulation and compute the achievable rate expressions for discrete constellations. Based on these expressions, we propose and evaluate two receiver architectures: one based on successive interference cancellation (SIC) and a non-SIC decoder. Both designs exhibit comparable performance, and the combination of polarization diversity and RSMA provides the system with significant flexibility to adapt to different channel conditions when serving both users, while the non-SIC decoder enables a simpler hardware implementation. We then present a prototype implementation of the proposed design, operating at a carrier frequency of 25 GHz, and evaluate it by measuring the symbol error rate (SER) of the different data streams under various signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and polarization diversity conditions. The obtained measurements show good agreement with software simulations, thereby validating the system implementation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first mmWave RSMA prototype reported in the literature and the first to exploit polarization diversity. Furthermore, given the selected carrier frequency, the proposed design may also find applicability in the upper portion of the envisioned FR3 band (7-24 GHz).

papers.title: AutoRSR: Automated Real-to-Sim-to-Real Data Generation for Scalable Robot Learning
papers.summary: Scaling embodied robot learning requires large and diverse manipulation datasets, but collecting real-world demonstrations remains expensive in human effort and robot time. Simulation provides a scalable alternative, yet converting a real workspace into a robot-learning-ready environment still requires substantial manual effort for object extraction, asset processing, coordinate calibration, and trajectory specification. We present AutoRSR, a highly automated real-to-sim-to real framework that converts scanned real-world workspaces into reusable embodied simulation assets and scalable manipulation data. Given multi-view observations, robot states, and open-vocabulary semantic queries, AutoRSR reconstructs the workspace, extracts individual object assets, and automatically registers the reconstructed scene to the robot base frame at metric scale. Starting from a small number of reference motions, AutoRSR then generates executable manipulation trajectories and scales them through trajectory interpolation and domain randomization. After workspace scanning and semantic queries, the remaining pipeline requires no manual object annotation, scene-to-robot calibration, or robot teleoperation. Across three real-world manipulation tasks, policies trained on 1K automatically generated episodes per task achieve 73.3--86.7% real-world success rates, comparable to pi 0.5 trained from 150 human teleoperated demonstrations, while reducing the human time required for data generation by an order of magnitude. These results demonstrate that real-world observations can be converted into metrically aligned, executable, and scalable simulation data with substantially reduced human effort.

papers.title: Read, Parse, Describe: Unified Document Parsing with Visual Element Description Generation
papers.summary: Document understanding systems are typically evaluated as separate components via layout analysis, optical text recognition, reading-order prediction, and image captioning. This separation leaves scientific figures, captions, and visual semantics weakly connected, and fails to measure whether a model can produce a single page-level parse that is both structurally faithful and semantically accessible. We introduce Read-Parse-Describe, a unified dataset for document parsing with visual element description generation. Given a page image, models are required to output an ordered list of layout elements containing bounding boxes, semantic labels, reading-order indices, recognized textual content, and alternative text descriptions for visual elements. The benchmark is built from 2,402 documents, comprising 18,163 continuous pages, 125,218 layout elements, and 11,338 visual instances. Besides, we further propose a plug-and-play space-awareness enhancer that reuses multi-layer visual features and injects grid-aware spatial guidance into vision-language tokens for layout-aware generation. Experiments across end-to-end VLMs and pipeline parsers show that existing systems still struggle to jointly recover reading order and visual semantics, while our enhanced model achieves strong joint performance. These results highlight the need to move beyond isolated document parsing modules toward unified models that jointly read, parse, and describe complex documents. The new dataset and code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yufanchen96/RPD

papers.title: TreeFlex: Agents Navigating Their Own Search Trees
papers.summary: A ReAct-style agent accumulates observations, intermediate results, and failed attempts in a single context. As this context grows, stale and off-path information consumes its limited capacity and obscures relevant evidence, making focused reasoning increasingly difficult. We introduce TreeFlex, a framework in which the agent's own policy decides where to search. The agent records each intermediate state, with a short summary, as a node in a search tree maintained by the harness. The policy is a single language model that acts in two roles. In the Reflection role, it has a global view of the tree through these summaries and picks a node to resume, together with an instruction. In the Execution role, the harness restores the path that led to that node, and the model carries out the instruction with the usual task tools until it saves a new node or proposes a solution, which Reflection then approves or sends back to another node. Through these choices, the policy decides whether to deepen the current line, branch from or revisit an earlier state, verify a proposal, or stop, without a fixed traversal order or a score for each node. We train navigation, task actions, checkpointing, and proposal review jointly with a tree-aware adaptation of GRPO, using task-level outcome rewards augmented by process rewards. After small-scale RL of a 4B model, with the same active-context limit for all methods, TreeFlex reaches 48.8% accuracy on a challenging deep-research benchmark, versus 41.5% for flat ReAct and 42.8% for FoldAgent, and its Pass@8 is about ten points higher than either. On SWE-bench Verified, with all three systems trained with RL from the same 9B model, TreeFlex resolves 54.9% of tasks, versus 43.3% for FoldAgent and 45.2% for its step-wise variant.

papers.title: VIGOR-MPC: Vision-Guided Objective Regulation MPC
papers.summary: Controlling an agent in an environment solely perceived through onboard vision is challenging: perception yields noisy, variable-length, and partially occluded context, while onboard compute is shared between perception and control, limiting the planning horizon executable in real time. We propose VIGOR-MPC, a modular student-teacher framework, agnostic to the perception pipeline, which addresses reference tracking across navigation tasks by distilling a privileged, field-of-view-aware long-horizon MPC into a computationally lightweight short-horizon MPC whose cost parameters are determined online from vision. The teacher operates in simulation with full state knowledge and a multi-trajectory formulation that guarantees the agent can stay within its field of view. The student observes only the noisy, occluded context produced by a perception module and learns, via a multi-level recurrent mapping, to infer cost parameters that aim to recover the teacher's behavior despite missing information. We evaluate VIGOR-MPC on vision-based autonomous racing in simulation and on hardware. Using only onboard perception of the track, VIGOR-MPC generalizes to tracks unseen during training and approaches the lap times of the privileged long-horizon teacher while reducing per-step computation by over 90%.

papers.title: IRAC-Excess Galaxies in the NIRSpec Wide Survey: physical properties of bright EELGs at $z\sim7$ and implications for Reionization
papers.summary: We present an analysis of 23 Spitzer/IRAC excess galaxies at $5.66 < z < 7.64$, observed as part of the NIRSpec Wide GTO survey. With NIRSpec PRISM spectroscopy, we measure a median rest-frame [OIII]$+\rm{H}β$ EW $=1583$~Å, consistent with predictions from the pre-JWST selection and we identify $17/23$ $(\sim74\%)$ of our sample as extreme emission line galaxies (EELGs), based on a selection of [OIII]$+\rm{H}β$ EW $\geq1000$~Å. The typical EELG is powered by star-formation rather than active galactic nuclei (AGN) based on their line widths, line ratios and absence of high-ionization lines, though we cannot exclude an AGN contribution in a few individual sources. We find that our luminous ($\langle M_\mathrm{UV}\rangle=-20.7$) EELG sample is characterised by sub-solar metallicities $(7.38 < \rm 12 + \log(O/H) < 8.12)$, young stellar populations ($t_\star \sim 20$ Myr), and enhanced ionizing photon production efficiencies, with median $\log_{10}(ξ_\mathrm{ion}/\mathrm{erg}^{-1}~\mathrm{Hz}) = 25.62$. We find that more UV luminous ($\sim L_\mathrm{UV, z=7}^\ast$) EELGs exhibit systematically lower O32 ratios than fainter ($\sim 0.1\times L_\mathrm{UV}^\ast$) EELGs at fixed [OIII]$+\rm{H}β$ EW, indicating less extreme radiation fields and/or lower gas densities than their fainter counterparts. Furthermore, bright EELGs exhibit low neutral hydrogen column densities, consistent with a scenario in which they have largely ionized their circumgalactic medium (CGM). Despite this, we find very low Lyman-$α$ escape fractions ($<2$\%), suggesting these systems reside in relatively small ($\lesssim 0.25$~pMpc) ionized regions of the intergalactic medium (IGM), possibly suggesting that bright galaxies have a minor contribution to reionization.

papers.title: Dynamic morphing of non-Euclidean active shells enabled by flutter under a steady stimulus
papers.summary: Synthetic active surfaces are usually designed to attain a prescribed static configuration, with dynamic shape changes typically requiring modulation of the actuation. We show that thin active shells can instead sustain dynamic morphing under a steady stimulus by harnessing flutter instability. We focus on polyelectrolyte hydrogel shells immersed in a viscous fluid and subjected to a constant and uniform electric field, and specialize the non-Euclidean framework for thin structures to account for field-induced activity through a spontaneous curvature evolving in time with the system configuration. Examining elliptic plates and cylindrical shells as test cases, we integrate linear stability analyses with nonlinear simulations to first locate the onset of flutter and then unveil the resulting dynamics, characterized by thrust-generating shape changes. In all cases, the emergent behavior stems from the interplay between active reconfiguration and elasticity in the fluid environment. For plates, the problem is purely flexural in the linear regime, while the competition between bending and stretching becomes crucial in selecting the ensuing shapes and swimming trajectories at large deformations. Conversely, for cylindrical shells bending and stretching are coupled at all levels, with the latter becoming essential to sustain flutter. Experiments on millimeter-sized hydrogel plates provide tangible support for our theoretical findings through shape reconstructions performed by combining digital image correlation with optical stereo microscopy. Flutter thus offers a route to untethered soft robotic and microfluidic devices based on active shells and operating under a stimulus carrying neither an intrinsic frequency nor a characteristic length scale.

papers.title: Anuvani-Diarization: Zero Shot Speaker Diarization and Annotation Conventions Across 22 Languages
papers.summary: India's 22 scheduled languages are spoken by over a billion people in conversations that mix languages, often within one turn, overlap freely, and take place over telephones, in meetings, and in media. Knowing who spoke when, the task of speaker diarization, is essential to speech applications for such conversation: voice agents conversing with several people at once, speaker attributed transcription of meetings and calls, contact center analytics, and media monitoring. We present a systematic study of speaker diarization across all 22 languages on IndicDiarBench and introduce Anuvani-Diarization, which adapts a self-supervised end-to-end segmentation model to Indian conversation with uncertainty aware silver supervision. Evaluated zero shot alongside nine recent diarization systems, it reaches a duration weighted diarization error rate (DER) of 16.78% on all 1,164 recordings, the lowest of all systems we ran and second only to the best published result (16.0%), and leads the three strongest rivals in 14 of 22 languages. It matches its parent on six international benchmarks. We also show that the benchmark's utterance level annotation convention is a hidden variable worth 1.9 to 4.1 DER points, depending on the system, and that a convention learned from other Indian transcriptions does not transfer.

papers.title: Thermalization of the Primordial Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background
papers.summary: It is conventionally believed that the Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background (SGWB) from inflation provides information about the earliest universe. However, in this Letter, we present a different picture. Our analysis starts from the observation that the inflation-predicted spectrum implies gravitons reside in high-occupation states, which significantly enhances their self-interactions and triggers rapid thermalization. We show that approximately $80\%$ of the primordial gravitons participate in this thermalization, forming a Bose--Einstein distribution and thereby erasing the primordial information. Evaluated using typical inflation parameters, this thermalized spectrum yields a present-day peak frequency of $f_{0, \text{peak}}^{(\text{th})} \sim 1.4 \times 10^8 \, \mathrm{Hz}$ in the hundred-megahertz band with a peak amplitude of $Ω_{0, \text{peak}}^{(\text{th})} \sim 3.5 \times 10^{-13}$. Due to the sharp drop-off away from the peak, the resulting spectrum lies beyond the reach of low-frequency observatories like PTAs, LISA, and LIGO, but remains uniquely accessible to high-frequency detectors such as microwave cavity resonators and dielectric haloscopes.

papers.title: Measurement of Born cross sections of $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.5-4.9 GeV and partial wave analysis at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.773 GeV
papers.summary: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at BEPCII corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 44.6 $\rm fb^{-1}$, we present the first measurement of the Born cross sections for the process $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. at fifty-six center-of-mass energies between 3.51 and 4.95~GeV. By fitting the dressed cross sections of $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. with the assumption of a power-law function plus a charmonium(-like) resonance, i.e., $ψ(3770)$, $ψ(4040)$, $ψ(4160)$, $Y(4230)$, $Y(4360)$, $ψ(4415)$, $ψ(4500)$, $Y(4660)$ or $ψ(4710)$, no significant charmonium(-like) state decaying into $pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. is observed. The product of branching fractions and electronic partial widths including their upper limits at the 90\% confidence level are provided for each decay. In addition, a partial wave analysis of the process $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.773 GeV is performed to investigate $N^{*}$, $Λ^{*}$ and $Σ^{*}$ resonances in the $K^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ and $pK^{-}$ invariant mass spectra. Significant contributions are found from the $Λ(1520)$, $Σ(1670)$, $Σ(1915)$, $N(1900)$, $N(2300)$ and $N(2570)$. The masses, widths and production fractions for each component are determined.

papers.title: Delay-Enabled Adaptive Learning of Time-Varying Parameters
papers.summary: This paper proposes a novel adaptive learning method for unknown time-varying parameters by deliberately incorporating a delay into the parameter update. Specifically, a conventional adaptive estimator is augmented with only one additional dynamic state, which estimates the parameter variation rate from the difference between current and previous parameter estimates. The method fundamentally changes the influence of time variation on estimation performance: the resulting estimation error is governed by the second derivative of the unknown parameter rather than its first derivative. Under persistent excitation, a small-gain analysis proves exponential stability of the complete estimation-error system and establishes explicit bounds for the parameter, state-prediction, and parameter-rate errors. In particular, accurate learning of linearly time-varying parameters and their unknown rates can be guaranteed with errors converging exponentially fast to zero. Numerical comparisons with conventional adaptive estimation and a recent timevarying parameter estimator demonstrate superior learning performance in the considered examples. The proposed delay-enabled adaptive estimator requires neither state derivatives nor any assumed model of parameter variation, and its implementation consists of one delayed difference and a first-order filter. These results thus provide a direct extension of adaptive learning from constant to time-varying parameters without sacrificing the simplicity of the conventional adaptive estimation mechanism.

papers.title: Hierarchical Gaussian Processes for Survey Weighting: Local Equivalent Weights in Structured Populations
papers.summary: Regression-based survey weighting connects model-based population estimation with design-based inference through equivalent weights. For nonlinear models, equivalent weights can be defined locally through the sensitivity of a poststratified population estimator. However, conventional regression models may inadequately capture nonlinear relationships and complex interactions across sparse poststratification cells. We develop a survey-weighting framework based on hierarchical Gaussian process (HGP) regression, combining structured group-level effects with kernel-based smoothing to share information across related cells. We derive Gaussian posterior prediction formulas that exploit the structured covariance representation to reduce computational costs. We also establish a uniform convergence result for the posterior predictive mean under stated regularity conditions and construct local equivalent weights by matching the first-order sensitivity of a plug-in poststratified estimand to that of a weighted average of fitted response means, with both derivatives taken with respect to the latent mean-scale vector. Simulations show that HGP achieves lower population-weighted prediction error under nonparametric structure, whereas logistic regression performs well under correct parametric specification. Additional analyses examine sample size, frame coverage, subgroup prediction, and population-mean agreement. An application to the Future of Families and Child Wellbeing Study illustrates the method. Overall, this work extends local equivalent-weight construction to nonparametric modeling and provides a computational framework and conditional theoretical results for survey weighting in structured, sparse populations.

papers.title: TacClaw-Infinity: A Large-Scale Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Dataset for Dexterous Manipulation
papers.summary: Large-scale robot learning increasingly relies on diverse human demonstrations, yet tactile manipulation data remain difficult to scale, and existing multimodal datasets often lack consistent quality control and structured supervision. We present TacClaw-Infinity, a large-scale structured Vision-Tactile-Language-Action (VTLA) dataset for contact-rich manipulation, collected with TacClaw, a tactile-enabled UMI-style handheld interface that records synchronized visual observations, fingertip tactile signals, and end-effector trajectories without requiring a target robot during data collection. TacClaw-Infinity is built through a distributed worldwide collection across homes, laboratories, industrial workplaces, retail stores, and outdoor environments including tasks contributed by academic and industrial collaborators. Together, these efforts yield over 10,000 hours, 1 million episodes, and 1 billion frames spanning more than 1,000 task types. We develop a scalable pipeline for trajectory reconstruction, multimodal quality control, embodiment-aware filtering, and structured annotation, covering contact-centric segmentation, subtask description, and spatial grounding. We validate TacClaw-Infinity at both the data and model levels: At the data level, we assess the collection interface, the action-space compatibility of the curated demonstrations, and the structured annotations, while for the model level, we demonstrate cross-embodiment transfer across three heterogeneous robots without robot-specific demonstrations.

papers.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation For Robot Policies
papers.summary: Reinforcement-learning policies for robot locomotion can fail at deployment when operating conditions shift (e.g., rough or slippery terrain, payload changes, sensing degradation), and retraining or manual recalibration is often infeasible under on-device latency and memory constraints. We study test-time adaptation (TTA) for robotic control: adapting a pretrained policy online and in a self-supervised manner during execution, without access to rewards. Our starting point is a lightweight baseline that updates only the actor using a frozen pretrained critic as a deployment-time performance surrogate. Building on this, we introduce TEMPO, a test-time entropy-regularized, memory-guided policy optimization method that stabilizes critic-driven updates under severe shift. TEMPO combines (i) an entropy-promoting regularizer on the critic's predictive distribution to mitigate overconfident extrapolation, and (ii) a score-based memory, inspired by prioritized replay, that prioritizes low-value ("hard") observations and applies importance sampling to focus limited computation on the most informative deployment conditions. Across Go1, Go2, and G1 in MuJoCo Playground under four representative shifts and multiple architectures, TEMPO yields consistent gains, reaching up to 80% improvement in a single-device setting. We further validate on a physical Unitree Go2 with an added calf payload, where fully on-device adaptation improves performance over the non-adapted baseline across real-world episodes.

papers.title: Building Sound Evaluation Practices for Rust-Based Security Frameworks
papers.summary: Background: Rust is a modern programming language known for its focus on usability, concurrency, and security. However, empirical studies reveal that Rust is still affected by software vulnerabilities, with hundreds of memory safety issues found in Rust programs, including Rust's standard library. As a result, additional tool-assisted security testing is crucial to enhance the security of Rust code. Evaluating such tools, however, is highly complex. While there is substantial research on evaluating C/C++ security frameworks, including test sets, serious issues in published evaluations have been identified, undermining their scientific soundness and reproducibility. In practice, selecting an inadequate implementation (e.g., a fuzzer) can lead to missed vulnerabilities ultimately compromising a program's security. Aims: Our methodology aims to help researchers to conduct scientifically sound evaluations in order to prevent similar issues with the evaluation of security tools and frameworks in the Rust ecosystem. Method: We systematically analyze existing evaluation literature to develop the first sound methodology for Rust based evaluations. Our guidelines provide enough flexibility to support a variety of use cases. To quantify the performance of a security tool, we introduce an automated approach to inject unsafe code coverage oracles, which require no forward porting, avoid overfitting, and allow updating test sets in the future. We also present methods to quantify the diversity of a Rust test set, ensuring that the results are applicable to a large set of existing Rust programs. We practically apply our methodology in our evaluation of the most popular Rust fuzzers. Results: We show the practical applicability of our design and conduct an evaluation with a diverse test set of 20 Rust projects. [...]

papers.title: Coherent and dissipative coupling of multiple photon-magnon hybrids in a chiral microwave resonator
papers.summary: We demonstrate control between level repulsion and level attraction of photon-magnon coupling spectra in a chiral microwave-photon resonator loaded with a 2 mm YIG sphere. By systematically varying the coupling mode volume via the YIG position and the dc-field orientation, we tune the ratio between coherent and dissipative coupling strengths, $J/Γ$, and thereby switch between level repulsion and level attraction in the hybrid spectra. Full-wave electromagnetic and magnetization-dynamics simulations reveal multiple photon-magnon hybrid modes with distinct spatial overlap factors, which quantitatively account for gap sizes and their angular dependence. Strong nonreciprocity appears near $J/Γ\approx 1$, yielding 28.6 dB isolation ratio in agreement with a unified single-bath input-output model and full-wave simulations. Angular dependence of spectral characterization confirms a picture of the chirality-selection rule and our method of geometric tuning might be useful for considering reconfigurable on-chip isolators.

papers.title: Making Weak Interlayer Excitons Absorb: Manipulating the Effective Oscillator Strength via Purcell Engineering of Critical Coupling
papers.summary: Interlayer excitons (IXs) in transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers possess unique dipolar properties, providing a path for exploring correlated many-body phases, electrically tunable dipole-dipole interactions, and long-range exciton transport. However, the large electron-hole separation underlying their dipolar character also results in a significantly reduced oscillator strength, limiting their direct optical interaction with light, and thus the direct probing of their dynamics and many-body interactions. Here, we show that by using Purcell engineering of critical coupling, a weak interlayer transition can absorb as strongly as the dominant intralayer transition, despite its much smaller intrinsic oscillator strength. Using this approach, in an open cavity architecture we demonstrate an order of magnitude IX absorption modulation in bilayer and trilayer MoS2, with doubling of the IX to A-exciton interaction strength weight from ~23% to ~53%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in a tailored closed cavity architecture, the IX enhancement can reach beyond an order of magnitude, from ~5% to ~83% excitonic absorption, enabling IX absorption similar to intralayer excitons. An analytical description of the interaction is obtained via a closed-form transmission-line model which separates the excitonic and photonic contributions to the optical response, revealing how cavity architecture can be designed towards critical coupling. Our findings establish Purcell engineering of critical coupling as a general route to controlling and enhancing weak excitonic transitions.

papers.title: Extreme-Scale Super-Resolution of Homogeneous Turbulence from a Single Realization
papers.summary: Homogeneous turbulent flows exhibit recurring multiscale structures across spatially separated regions, suggesting that a single flow realization may contain sufficient information to learn representations of unresolved scales. We investigate this hypothesis through an extreme super-resolution framework in which a wide-activation deep super-resolution (WDSR) network is trained exclusively on overlapping patches extracted from a single high-resolution turbulent realization. Previously unseen flow fields are reconstructed through patchwise prediction followed by Hann-window-weighted overlap-add assembly. The framework is evaluated for two-dimensional homogeneous isotropic turbulence at super-resolution factors of x32 and x64, representing severe spatial under-resolution. Despite the limited training data, the proposed approach reconstructs coherent vortical structures and recovers fine-scale features more accurately than conventional interpolation. Spectral and statistical analyses further demonstrate improved recovery of high-wavenumber energy content and multiscale flow characteristics. To assess the effectiveness of exploiting internal spatial information, we compare the proposed framework against WDSR models trained on 1, 25, 50, and 100 complete high-resolution snapshots without patch extraction. This comparison distinguishes the benefits of localized learning from those associated with increasing the number of training realizations. The results demonstrate that exploiting spatial redundancy within a single turbulent realization enables accurate reconstruction of previously unseen flow fields, even under extreme spatial under-resolution.
