The fluctuations are built in following the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. The effect of space discretization into cells in numerical hydrodynamics on the spatial correlation of fluctuations is studied with the help of static structure factor. A difference from the continuum result is pointed out and systematically investigated. Time evolution of the ensuing fluctuations is examined and the Green-Kubo formula is used for the extraction of shear viscosity from the fluctuations. The extracted value is demonstrated to be the same as the input value of the shear viscosity for the simulations using Israel-Stewart equations. It is also shown that numerical regulators commonly used in the codes to ensure stability of the calculation severely spoil the fluctuations and break the fluctuation-dissipation theorem.

papers.title: From Mind Mapping to Dream Interpretation: Understanding Muslim Users' Engagement with GenAI Tools in Religious Context
papers.summary: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools are increasingly integrated into everyday life, including sensitive domains such as religion. Prior works examined alignment with religious values and discussed the potential risks. However, to gain empirical insights into the adoption of these tools in users' religious lives, in this study, we conducted an online survey with 178 Muslim participants in Bangladesh and collected 726 prompts on religious use cases, along with open-ended responses about using these tools in religious contexts. Using reflexive thematic analysis, we identify three key roles these tools play in users' religious lives: (1) religious assistants, (2) perceived religious scholars, and (3) faith counselors. However, participants expressed concerns about misguidance, overreliance, and violations of Islamic tradition, and reported adopting protective strategies to avoid these pitfalls. Based on these, we propose a set of design guidelines for faith-sensitive GenAI systems that would preserve religious boundaries while supporting religious practices.
authors: A. B. M. Alim Al Islam
papers.journal: International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction, HCII 2026

papers.title: How Safe Is ChatGPT Health Advice? Evidence from Real User Conversations in Four Global South Countries
papers.summary: People increasingly bring their health questions to ChatGPT, yet safety evaluations of LLM health advice rest almost entirely on clinician-authored vignettes, synthetic prompts, or simulated user profiles. The gap is widest for the Global South, where concerns about demographic bias and unsafe recommendations are well documented but have never been tested on real usage. We present, to our knowledge, the first demographically grounded safety evaluation of real-world health conversations with ChatGPT. From a consent-based data-donation corpus of 202,590 conversations from 1,252 users in India, Nigeria, Brazil, and Pakistan (December 2022 to February 2026), each linked to self-reported age and gender, we identify 15,555 health conversations, classify their health intent using an LLM classifier adapted from an established taxonomy, and score response safety under both a context-blind and a user-context-aware rubric. Roughly one in five health conversations receives a high-risk rating. Risk concentrates in symptom and condition queries and recurs through identifiable failure modes: unsafe medication or dosage guidance, harmful self-diagnosis, missing safety warnings, encouraging over-reliance on the model, and failure to refer users to professionals. Supplying the user's own accumulated context raises the high-risk share by 13-17 percentage points, and about one in four conversations rated safe in isolation turns out to be unsafe for the specific person asking. Safety evaluations built on synthetic cases are likely to miss these harms.

papers.title: STAMP as a topology-aware molecular language for fragment-level learning and editing
papers.summary: Molecular fragments provide chemically meaningful units, but existing molecular languages rarely make their locations and connections explicit for editing. Here we introduce STAMP (Sequential Tree Attachment-based Motif-Preserving representation), a topology-aware molecular language that connects fragment-level representation learning with precise structural editing. STAMP separately encodes motif identity, attachment sites and tree topology, making fragments reusable across contexts and subtrees directly accessible. Learned representations capture motif similarity and recurring transformations, and lower activity-cliff prediction error on 23 of 30 targets versus a matched SMILES encoder. Compatible subtree operations support scaffold-preserving optimization, ranking first among six methods on 15 of 23 benchmark objectives. A deterministic compiler enables frozen language models to act on indexed fragments, improving molecular editing, optimization, transformation transfer and change identification by 9 to 56 percentage points over plain SMILES. Together, these results establish an executable molecular language in which learned chemical units remain directly operable during design.

papers.title: How Well Do LLMs Perform in Peer Review? Evidence from Finance and Accounting
papers.summary: Referees increasingly use large language models (LLMs), while finance and accounting journals disagree about whether to allow it. We ask which part of a referee's job the models can do. GPT-4o, whose training data end before the 2024 conference season, referees the papers presented at the 2024 AFA and NBER finance meetings, and we compare its verdicts with publication in the top-three finance journals over the next two years. Papers the model scores one standard deviation higher are 44\% more likely to be published, net of author reputation. The result is not driven by look-ahead bias, as the model does not recall the outcomes. The information comes from its judgements of correctness and exposition. Its judgements of originality and significance carry none, and a referee guide that stresses importance does not help. The split between correctness and contribution holds for accounting papers and for a newer model, GPT-5. LLMs can check whether research is right, but not whether it matters. The technical check can go to the model, while the judgement of contribution stays with people.

papers.title: Risk Measures for the Climate Transition Age: Why Symmetric Risk Budgets are unlikely to mitigate two-dimensionally asymmetric Climate Change risks
papers.summary: The most widely used investment risk measures - variance, standard deviation, and tracking error - treat upside deviations as equally undesirable as downside losses. In stable markets with assumed symmetric return distributions, this simplification is potentially harmless. In the climate transition age, it is not. Climate risk is two-dimensionally asymmetric, across assets and over time. Both dimensions are negatively skewed against investors. Hence, climate transition investment strategies deliberately deviate from benchmarks that reflect an insufficiently decarbonising global economy. When fiduciaries enforce tracking error budgets that penalise outperformance just as heavily as underperformance, they inadvertently constrain exactly the portfolio return opportunities that climate-aware investing seeks. We argue that replacing symmetric deviation-based risk measures with their downside-only counterparts - semi-variance, standard risk and trailing error - resolves this conflict without sacrificing any fiduciary discipline. The distinction is not merely semantic: as the gap between climate transition trajectories and market benchmarks widens over the coming decades, symmetric risk budgets will become binding constraints on transition strategies well before actual investment risk warrants it. We propose specific changes to mandate design that would allow institutional investors to pursue climate transition opportunities within genuinely risk-aware (rather than deviation-averse) frameworks.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 1 figure, 9 equations| Keywords: climate change mitigation, Climate Transition Benchmarks, deviation, fiduciary duty, Paris-Aligned Benchmarks, risk, standard risk,

papers.title: Understanding the "Why": Investigating the Design of Privacy Support Tools (PSTs) through the Lens of Psychological Needs
papers.summary: Privacy Support Tools (PSTs) help users control their digital data, but face low adoption due to resignation and overwhelm. While current regulations aim to enhance privacy control, users still struggle to manage their privacy. To address this, we explore how PSTs can be designed for long-term adoption by applying the theoretical lens of psychological needs, as their fulfillment motivates users to use a digital product. We conducted in-depth interviews with 15 users and identified Security, Autonomy, and Competence as key psychological needs. From our results, we derive implications and recommendations for the need-sensitive design of PSTs.

papers.title: Portfolio Decarbonization under Incomplete Carbon and Transition Information
papers.summary: We study dynamic portfolio decarbonization under incomplete information about firms' carbon intensities and the underlying transition state. The investor maximizes expected utility of terminal wealth net of a penalty on perceived cumulative financed emissions. Asset returns and carbon intensities depend on a stochastic transition factor, while the investor may need to infer the current transition state, its long-run mean and firms' carbon intensities from market observations and periodic noisy disclosures. The optimal strategy combines a Merton-type component with climate-dependent expected-return adjustments, a direct carbon intensity penalty and intertemporal hedging demands associated with stochastic carbon intensities and learning. In a numerical application, incomplete information has limited effects on welfare and target satisfaction when prior beliefs are well specified. By contrast, biased beliefs generate welfare losses in either direction but asymmetric environmental consequences: optimistic and pessimistic beliefs induce opposite portfolio tilts and therefore affect the probability of exceeding the cumulative emissions target differently.

papers.title: The influence of decay in dynamic models of gene regulatory networks
papers.summary: We investigate the influence of decay rates on the dynamics of three-dimensional gene regulatory networks modeled by nonlinear differential equations with logistic sigmoidal regulatory functions. Particular attention is paid to the existence, location, and stability of equilibrium points in systems involving numerous interacting parameters. An explicit analytical representation of a central equilibrium is obtained under suitable relations between the regulatory weights, thresholds, and decay coefficients, allowing its location to be determined without solving the corresponding nonlinear algebraic system numerically. General formulas for the characteristic polynomial of the linearized system are derived, and spectral conditions for instability are established for several classes of regulatory interactions. We demonstrate how variations in decay rates can change the number and stability of equilibria, transform oscillatory dynamics, and influence the emergence or suppression of complicated attractors. The possibility of chaotic behavior is investigated through eigenvalue configurations, Lyapunov exponents, and the Kaplan-Yorke dimension. Numerical examples illustrate the sensitivity of the dynamics to decay parameters, including the suppression of previously observed chaotic behavior. The results provide an analytical framework for investigating equilibrium configurations, stability transitions, and complex dynamics in parametrized gene regulatory networks.

papers.title: Femtoscopic parameters of pion emission sources in EPOS4 Au+Au collisions from 7.7 to 200 GeV
papers.summary: Three-dimensional femtoscopy probes the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The collision-energy dependence of Lévy source parameters may reveal the evolution of strongly interacting matter and possible signatures of the QCD phase diagram. We previously studied the excitation function of three-dimensional Lévy source parameters for pion pairs in Au+Au collisions with EPOS4, analyzing the pair-distance distribution \(D(ρ)\) through one-dimensional projections. Here, we analyze the full three-dimensional source distribution and correlation function directly. We construct \(D(ρ_{\rm out},ρ_{\rm side},ρ_{\rm long})\) as a 3D histogram, transform it into \(C(q_{\rm out},q_{\rm side},q_{\rm long})\) using a Fast Fourier Transform, and fit the correlation function with the analytic Lévy formula. This approach can reduce biases arising when one-dimensional projections are used to describe a non-elliptical source. We apply the method across the RHIC Beam Energy Scan range and compare the extracted energy dependence with results from the projection-based method and recent UrQMD calculations. We focus on the out-side observables \(R_{\rm diff}^{2}=R_{\rm out}^{2}-R_{\rm side}^{2}\) and \(R_{\rm out}/R_{\rm side}\), whose different energy dependences in EPOS4 and UrQMD may illuminate the roles of emission duration and source dynamics. This work establishes a direct three-dimensional framework for comparison with future femtoscopic measurements and for exploring possible non-monotonic structures associated with the QCD phase diagram.

papers.title: An efficient and flexible generalization of transit compartment models for delayed biological processes
papers.summary: Transit compartment models are widely used in pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics to represent delayed biological processes such as absorption, maturation, cellular proliferation, and treatment-induced toxicity. This transit compartment formulation imposes an artificial relationship between the mean and variance of the delay distribution, as the number of transit compartment must be integer-valued number of transit compartments. Consequently, estimating the number of compartments from experimental data leads to mixed-integer optimization problems that artificially constrain model dynamics and bias parameter inference. However, these transit compartment models are mathematically equivalent to distributed delay differential equations with Erlang delay kernels. We leverage a hypoexponential generalization of these distributed delay differential equations that preserves the familiar ordinary differential equation structure while allowing the mean and variance of the delay distribution to be estimated directly as real-valued parameters. This approach does not increase the number of inferred parameters and can be immediately implemented as a straightforward modification of existing transit compartment models. We demonstrate the approach using models of viral eclipse phases, lymphocyte proliferation, and chemotherapy-induced neutropenia. Across these examples, the hypoexponential formulation provides comparable or improved fits relative to Erlang transit models and substantially reduces computational cost by avoiding grid search over compartment numbers. This framework provides a practical approach to estimate biologically meaningful delay distributions in quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models.

papers.title: Exact solution of adiabatic time dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov inertia for fission
papers.summary: An efficient method to exactly compute the adiabatic time-dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov collective vibrational inertias typical of fission is proposed. The method uses the quasiparticle finite amplitude method to invert the stability matrix of linear response. A comparison with other approaches, such as the exact generator coordinate method inertia and the associated cranking non-perturbative approximation, is conducted. It is found that the behaviour as a function of the collective variable (mass quadrupole moment) is essentially the same in the four cases considered, and substantially differs from the commonly used perturbative approach. It is also found that the magnitudes of the inertias are to a good extent related by single factors that seem to be connected with the effective mass of the energy density functional used.

papers.title: Exploring Object Recall in an Object-Rich AR Office Scene
papers.summary: Augmented reality (AR) changes how users perceive and attend to their surroundings. Prior work suggests AR can reduce attention to the physical world, but it remains unclear whether this holds in environments dense with both virtual and physical objects, and which factors most affect object recall. This study examines recall in a mixed-reality office scene after an object-selection task, testing object-level factors (virtuality, size), context-level factors (semantic congruency, saliency), and user-level factors (cueing, dual tasking). Cueing informed participants of a later recall test, while dual tasking added cognitive load through a secondary audio task. Virtual objects were recalled more accurately than physical ones. Cueing produced a modest improvement in recall of present objects. Using playback software to reconstruct each participant's view throughout the trials, we computed object-level saliency and found a weak positive correlation with recall, slightly stronger than the effects of virtuality, but not reaching statistical significance. These findings have implications for AR interface design and for building mixed-reality environments that better support cognition during real-world tasks.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 9 figures. Accepted to IEEE ISMAR 2026 and published in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (TVCG), Vol. 32, 2026

papers.title: Sense-Making phase transition framework for Affect
papers.summary: Contemporary accounts of affect emphasize different perspectives, ranging from the regulation of bodily states in allostatic approaches to the relational and sense-making character stressed by enactive theories. Here, we show that affect can be made explicit within the sense-making phase transition framework previously introduced for the perception of an inner sensation. Within this same formal structure, each stable minimum of the sense-making potential defines an affective state: its position determines valence, while its depth determines arousal. Affect therefore is not introduced as an independent ingredient, but emerges as the associated state in the valence-arousal space, providing a link between allostatic and enactive approaches to affect. This formulation distinguishes valence intensity from arousal, allows for dominant and secondary affective states, and naturally accommodates mixed-valence configurations beyond a strictly bipolar description. Revisiting representative landscapes of the model, we show how neutral, uncertain, polarized, and mixed-valence regimes arise as a function of contextual sensory information, learned historical evaluation, and externally supplied information. We further show that the resulting valence-arousal relation provides a theoretical basis for the upper-open V-shaped organization discussed in the affect literature, while also opening a natural route toward a dynamical description of affect and emotions.

papers.title: Finite-Temperature Equations of State for Neutron-Star Mergers within the Quark Mean-Field Model
papers.summary: We extend the quark mean-field (QMF) model to finite temperature and systematically investigate the thermodynamic properties of uniform nuclear matter, using the relativistic mean-field (RMF) model as a reference. For each model, we consider two parameter sets calibrated to the same selected nuclear-matter saturation properties but with different nucleon Dirac effective-mass ratios at saturation. We examine the effective nucleon mass and the composition of $β$-equilibrium matter, together with the free energy, energy density, pressure, entropy, and heat capacities of symmetric nuclear matter, pure neutron matter, and $β$-equilibrium matter. The QMF and RMF models exhibit similar qualitative trends, but their predictions increasingly differ at high density, where the effective masses have distinct density dependences. These differences are particularly evident in the thermal pressure and thermal index. For the two parameter sets considered in this work, we further provide compact analytical representations of the thermal index, $Γ_{\rm th}(ρ_{\rm b},T,β)$ over baryon densities of 0.08-1.0 $\rm fm^{-3}$, temperatures of 5-100 MeV, and isospin asymmetries of 0-1. The fits reproduce the numerical results with an accuracy better than $2\%$ and can be directly implemented in binary neutron-star merger simulations. This study establishes a finite-temperature extension of the QMF framework and provides a basis for future assessments of how a quark-structure-based description of nuclear matter affects thermal support and post-merger dynamics in binary neutron-star mergers.

papers.title: CompanionSafe: From Multi-turn Safety Evaluation to Guardrails for AI Companions
papers.summary: AI companions provide users with emotional support and ongoing companionship, but their sustained relational interactions also introduce distinct safety risks. Prior work largely targets general harms or specific companion platforms and risk categories, while relying on manually collected conversations, limiting scalable and user-grounded evaluation and mitigation. To address this, we introduce CompanionSafe, a unified evaluation-to-mitigation framework for AI companion safety. Its evaluation component, CompanionEval, provides scalable multi-turn evaluation by constructing 1,300 relationally grounded settings from diverse personas, matched companion characters, and dialogue scenarios across four turn tiers. Its mitigation component, CompanionGuard, converts benchmark-exposed failures into turn-localized supervision for companion-specific risk detection. Our results show that even strong LLMs and existing guard models remain vulnerable to companion-specific relational harms, while both closed- and open-source models exhibit increasing safety risks as interactions become longer. Together, CompanionEval and CompanionGuard form a practical evaluation-to-mitigation loop for AI companion safety, turning relational safety failures exposed during multi-turn interaction into supervision for companion-specific guardrails.
papers.comment: 40 pages, 33 figures, Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/AI45Lab/CompanionSafe

papers.title: Color Lorentz force on a transversely polarized quark in the nucleon
papers.summary: The $x^2$ moment of the genuine twist-3 component of the unpolarized scalar parton distribution function $e(x)$ is related to the average transverse color Lorentz force experienced by a transversely polarized quark in an unpolarized nucleon. This higher-twist quantity probes quark--gluon correlations and provides unique insight into the nonperturbative dynamics of quantum chromodynamics. For the first time, we study the corresponding off-forward matrix element and derive its Lorentz-covariant decomposition in terms of generalized form factors. We calculate these form factors from light-front wave functions obtained by solving the light-front Hamiltonian eigenvalue problem within the Basis Light-Front Quantization framework. Their Fourier transforms provide a spatial picture of the transverse color forces in impact-parameter space. In particular, $\mathscr{F}_2$, whose forward limit is directly related to the twist-3 matrix element $e_2$, can be interpreted as the impact-parameter-space representation of the Boer--Mulders force, providing an intuitive spatial picture of the final-state interaction mechanism underlying the Boer--Mulders effect.

papers.title: Covariant approach to allowed beta decay
papers.summary: We propose a Lorentz-covariant on-shell formalism for allowed nuclear beta decay. Nuclear matrix elements are organized in a systematic effective field theory expansion in the recoil momentum, with the dependence on nuclear spin and polarization encoded in little-group-covariant structures. In this language, we construct the most general standard and exotic currents for allowed transitions through first recoil order. We then derive the differential decay distribution encoded in a set of Lorentz-invariant form factors. Specializing to the rest frame of the parent nucleus, we relate our parameters to those used in the traditional beta-decay literature and in nucleon- and quark-level effective field theories. The formalism provides a natural framework for extensions to higher recoil orders, radiative corrections, and forbidden transitions.

papers.title: Lossless Reductions and Hybrid Sampling for Phylogeny Using the Maximum Compatibility Criterion
papers.summary: Maximum compatibility provides a criterion for phylogenetic reconstruction in which the objective is to retain a maximum set of mutually compatible characters. For binary characters, pairwise compatibility can be represented by a weighted graph whose vertices correspond to characters and whose edges connect compatible pairs. A leading algorithm by Cherry [BMC Bioinformatics, 18(1):127, 2017] uses this representation to identify maximum compatible character sets as maximum weight cliques. We formulate the problem as maximum weight independent set enumeration on the complement graph and use deterministic postprocessing to map sampled bit strings to maximal feasible solutions. To explore the prospects of quantum computational advantage, we further construct bespoke correction-in-the-loop Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm instances and find that traditional Lagrange multiplier choices may not be optimal for the enumeration problem on noisy devices. We also introduce lossless graph reductions with reconstruction rules that preserve the complete set of optimal solutions. Our results indicate that graph reduction and sampling can be effectively combined to address the enumeration bottleneck in maximum compatibility phylogeny, while retaining exact reconstruction when the residual optimum set is completely resolved. We enhance Cherry's approach to maximum compatibility by introducing graph reduction techniques and quantum sampling. Our classical benchmarks show a clear difference between finding one optimum and recovering the optimum set in practice. We demonstrate the utility of our methods on graphs constructed from SARS-CoV-2 sequences.

papers.title: Rewiring of adult neural networks - learning from structural plasticity across multiple scales
papers.summary: Synaptic connections are continuously formed and eliminated even in adult neuronal networks. This process - called structural plasticity - allows networks to change their topology to learn and adapt to their environment or compensate for lesions. Yet, in contrast to synaptic plasticity, structural plasticity is less well studied and understood. We here present the current state of knowledge as well as open problems in the field along three guiding questions: (1) What regulates structural plasticity in biological neural networks? (2) What are the functional consequences and advantages of structural plasticity in adult neural networks? (3) How can our understanding of structural plasticity be translated into clinical and technological applications? We argue that understanding structural plasticity is a problem involving multiple temporal and spatial scales. Solving this problem thus requires collaborative efforts of experimentalists, theoreticians as well as computational modelers, and has the potential for comprehensive neuroscientific insights that can guide the development of medical applications, artificial neural networks as well as neuromorphic computing.

papers.title: On integrability of local utility maximizing strategies
papers.summary: In stochastic control problems involving optimal portfolio choice, one often seeks an optimizer of some local criterion (dynamic programming value function) generated by some global criterion (e.g., expected utility). The local optimizer then typically acts as a stochastic integrand with respect to some multivariate stochastic process (e.g., asset prices). This paper takes a closer look at local criteria in the form of ``local expected utility''. Since the existence of the local optimizer can be established under very mild conditions, it is crucial to understand under what circumstances the local optimizer has good integrability properties. It is shown that the reasonable asymptotic elasticity condition of Kramkov and Schachermayer (1999) applied to the local utility function plays a key role in this context.

papers.title: Contribution of incomplete fusion to the evaporation residue cross sections in the $^{30}$Si$+^{186}$W reaction
papers.summary: The formation of the evaporation residues in the $^{30}$Si$+^{186}$W reaction leading to the compound nucleus $^{216}$Ra$^*$ has been studied in the framework of the dinuclear system (DNS) model. The capture, complete fusion, quasifission, and incomplete fusion cross sections have been calculated at the collision energies $E_{c.m.}=107.6-172.2$MeV by averaging over the orientation angles of the axial symmetry axes of the deformed $^{30}$Si and $^{186}$W nuclei. The incomplete fusion is considered as the breakup of the DNS with the emission of the $α$ particle from its very mass-asymmetric configuration, which is populated by the nucleon transfer in collisions with large orbital angular momentum. The survival probabilities of the excited $^{216}$Ra and of the conjugate nucleus $^{212}$Rn formed after the $α$-particle emission have been calculated using the statistical model. It is shown that the complete fusion is the main source of the evaporation residues at the lower collision energies, while above $E_{c.m.}=128$MeV the Rn isotopes formed in the incomplete fusion give more than half of the calculated evaporation residue cross section. The sum of both contributions describes the slow decrease of the measured total evaporation residue cross section at these energies, where the yield of the Ra isotopes decreases by an order of magnitude. The calculation of the de-excitation of $^{216}$Ra$^*$ with the emission of protons and $α$ particles shows that the contribution of the complete fusion to the cross sections of the isotopes $^{212}$Rn and $^{211}$Rn is negligible, and these isotopes are formed in the incomplete fusion. The fusion probability calculated for the partial waves $\ell\leq30\hbar$ is about 0.75 in comparison with the value $0.57\pm0.08$ extracted from the experimental data at the same collision energies.

papers.title: Spatial Kernel Restricted Canonical Correlation Analysis: Population Targets, Identifiability, and Stability
papers.summary: Relating observations of different categories across space requires methods that accommodate distinct sampling locations and spatial dependence. Spatial kernel restricted canonical correlation analysis (skrCCA) uses spatial weights to identify associated feature combinations across data categories. Here, we develop a statistical theory of its covariance form after feature reduction. Conditional on the observed locations and under a mean-zero model, the pairwise association matrices target kernel-weighted averages of cross-covariances. For prespecified directions, we derive the exact null variance under independence between blocks. We establish recovery and stability bounds in two- and multiblock settings under explicit population models, and show that exact cyclic updates have convergent objective values. The variance characterization shows how spatial weighting and within-block dependence jointly determine the effective information available for estimating association. The recovery bounds separate statistical and optimization error, relating stability to population separation and the strength of connections between blocks. These results clarify what fitted spatial association axes estimate and provide conditions under which they can be recovered reliably.

papers.title: The 3He(α,γ)7Be γ-ray angular distribution: measured, and calculated by effective field theory
papers.summary: The 3He(alpha,gamma)7Be reaction takes place in several distinct astrophysical scenarios. First, in solar hydrogen burning, 3He(alpha,gamma)7Be controls the competition between the pp-I chain, on the one hand, and the pp-II and -III chains, on the other hand. Its rate directly affects the solar model predictions for the well-measured 7Be and 8B solar neutrino fluxes, which can in principle be used as solar thermometer. Second, in Big Bang nucleosynthesis, 3He(alpha,gamma)7Be is the main production channel for primordial 7Li, the decay product of 7Be. Finally, the reaction is believed to produce radioactive 7Be in astrophysical novae. The cross section of this reaction has been studied previously using different methods, namely 7Be activation, 7Be recoil detection, and in-beam γ-ray detection. The latter studies have in many cases been performed with just one detector in close geometry. Here, for the first time a comprehensive measurement of the 3He(α,γ)7Be γ-ray angular distribution is reported. Altogether 22 high-purity germanium detectors were used, arranged at 27-145 degrees angle with respect to the beam direction. Data were taken at 442-1213 keV center-of-mass energy. In addition, one data point for the astrophysical S-factor was obtained with the activation method. The angular data are compared with the predictions from a hybrid theoretical approach, where the E1 transitions are modeled using a cluster-based effective field theory (EFT) while the M1 and E2 transitions within an EFT-inspired framework. Good agreement is found, if the interference among these multipolarities is taken into account in the theory.
papers.comment: Submitted to Phys. Rev. C as a Letter

papers.title: Structured SDEs for Realized GARCH: Continuous-Time Volatility Modelling and Component-Level Analysis
papers.summary: We propose a structured continuous-time stochastic volatility model for one-day-ahead integrated-variance forecasting. The model introduces a jointly evolving realized-measure state that feeds directly into latent variance dynamics, while correlated Brownian innovations capture return-linked dependence. Parameters are estimated through simulation-based predictive learning, and Monte Carlo simulation forecasts integrated variance. Across 17 equity indices, the proposed model shows strong out-of-sample performance relative to GARCH, GARCH-Itô, Realized GARCH, HAR, and HEAVY benchmarks under QLIKE, MSE, and MAE. Ablation results show that realized-measure feedback provides substantial incremental forecasting value within the proposed framework, while return-linked Brownian dependence contributes more modest complementary gains. The results support incorporating measurement-driven information directly into continuous-time latent volatility dynamics to improve integrated-variance forecasting.
papers.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on STODY

papers.title: ECG-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Targeted Electrocardiogram Waveform Evolution
papers.summary: Electrocardiogram (ECG) models need supervision that targets evolving weaknesses and remains faithful to waveform evidence. We introduce ECG-RSI, a recursive self-improvement framework combining verified waveform synthesis with feedback-guided intervention search. Signal remeasurement verifies waveform edits; construction errors guide generator repair, while learner errors motivate interventions compared on a separate selection set. Across seven benchmarks, three rounds raise Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's mean question-answering accuracy from 34.57% to 56.04% and mean classification F1 from 24.27 to 34.03. Across the retained trajectory, the preferred supervision shifts from direct reinforcement to confusion-focused contrasts. Continued feedback correction yields diminishing external gains. These results motivate separating error diagnosis from intervention selection and checking whether gains on the feedback set transfer to independent benchmarks.

papers.title: Understanding Gene Expression-to-Image Learning: Spatial Structure and Information Fidelity
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables cell-level analysis of biological heterogeneity, but learning effective representations from high-dimensional, unordered gene expression profiles remains challenging. Gene Expression-to-Image (GE2I) offers an effective learning strategy by arranging gene values on pixel grids for convolutional neural networks, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We study GE2I on full-transcriptome data while keeping the network and training procedure fixed. Our results reveal a trade-off between spatial smoothness and gene-level fidelity. Structured mappings produce smooth, low-frequency patterns that support faster early optimization, whereas assigning multiple genes to the same pixel obscures expression differences and can reduce predictive performance. This trade-off explains why random mappings can compete with structured layouts when many genes are represented. One-to-one gene-to-pixel assignment improves prediction across the tested visual backbones even when image smoothness decreases. We further find that the benefits of pretraining and augmentation depend on the backbone and mapping. These findings provide practical guidance for pixel allocation and the transfer of vision priors to gene expression data.

papers.title: MedEvo: Medical Reasoning Evolution through Knowledge Navigation
papers.summary: Medical multimodal reasoning models are typically trained on teacher-generated rationales, discarding the valid reasoning in students' own failed trajectories, while general-domain correction methods offer little guidance for errors in image reading, anatomical context, or differential diagnosis. We propose MedEvo, which uses medical knowledge, namely a tag taxonomy and error-type diagnosis, to navigate both trajectory repair and data selection. For each failed rollout, a gold-blind auditor locates the first consequential error and provides a minimal, answer-free hint; the same student retains the valid prefix and regenerates the erroneous suffix. After each round, MedEvo identifies capability gaps across medical tags on a held-out feedback set and prioritizes related questions for new rollouts and repairs. With supervised fine-tuning (SFT) alone, MedEvo raises Qwen3.5-9B mean accuracy across seven benchmarks from 65.57% to 69.12% (47.40% to 54.50% on the multimodal track of MedXpertQA (MedXpertQA-MM)), surpassing teacher-distillation SFT (66.93%). It also raises Qwen3.5-35B and Qwen3.5-397B mean accuracy from 67.91% to 73.04% and from 71.83% to 74.95%, respectively. Our analyses show that failed trajectories contain reasoning worth preserving, that repair success does not imply learning value, and that independent feedback is key to sustained improvement.

papers.title: E-Backtesting Expected Shortfall without Value-at-Risk Forecasts under Time-series Models
papers.summary: Expected Shortfall (ES) measures the average size of tail losses. Its sequential backtests typically also require a Value-at-Risk (VaR) forecast. We develop two e-backtesting methods using only observed losses and ES forecasts: one for iid losses only and the other for time series under an AR-GARCH conditional VaR structure. Under the stated assumptions, both control false rejections at any stopping time. For the time-series method, validity requires a fixed parameter--quantile pair representing the conditional VaR path and a positive report margin. The time-series statistic takes an infimum over possible parameter and VaR values. We choose the betting process $(λ_t)$ by maximizing an empirical growth rate averaged across candidate parameters. We compute the statistic by continuous VaR profiling on a dense parameter grid. For grid approximations, we prove convergence to the continuous infimum, together with convergence of the probability of false rejection, as the grid is refined over a fixed monitoring period. Lower and upper bounds for the VaR infimum on the parameter grid control the accuracy of the numerical profiling. Simulations, including ES reports that change from over-reporting to under-reporting, and an application to daily NASDAQ losses provide numerical comparisons with VaR--ES e-processes and fixed-sample ES backtests, assessing detection frequencies and the timing of rejections.

papers.title: AI Information Synthesis and Content Polarization
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) can synthesize dispersed information into balanced and informative content, raising the possibility that AI may help reduce polarization. We show that this promise can be undermined by the strategic response of content producers. We develop a game-theoretic model in which consumers acquire information to make downstream decisions, content producers allocate limited informational capacity between broadly valuable vertical information and horizontally differentiated information, and AI provides an alternative source of synthesized information. The effects of AI unfold in three phases as its reliability increases. When reliability is low, AI has no effect on the market. At intermediate levels, AI disciplines prices without attracting consumers or changing content. When AI becomes sufficiently reliable, consumers begin to substitute toward it, and content producers respond by shifting informational capacity away from the vertical dimension and toward horizontally differentiated content, thereby increasing content polarization. The mechanism operates through audience composition: AI attracts consumers who are less well matched to individual producers, leaving producers with stronger incentives to cater to their remaining audiences. The polarization effect intensifies with AI reliability but weakens with greater competition among content producers. Our findings highlight a potential wedge between AI's direct and equilibrium effects: a technology that provides consumers with more balanced information can indirectly make the broader content ecosystem more polarized.

papers.title: Octupole parton structure of spin-3/2 targets
papers.summary: In spin-$3/2$ targets, octupole polarization can reveal quark and gluon correlations beyond those probed by vector polarization and quadrupole alignment. Here, we construct the complete leading-twist gluon transverse-momentum-dependent distribution basis, with 32 independent coefficients for each specified Wilson-line and color structure. Fourteen of these describe octupole dependence in gluon number, helicity, and linear polarization. In heavy-quark-pair leptoproduction at small, nonzero pair imbalance, comparing target states with opposite octupoles and identical lower moments isolates the octupole contribution. Beam-helicity reversal and joint angular projections in target orientation and pair-imbalance azimuth can then separate all fourteen gluon octupole responses at leading-power Born order. We also derive the incoming-target quark responses in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering and Drell-Yan production. Time-reversal relations between distributions remain valid under symmetry-preserving renormalization and evolution, while predictions across processes require factorization formulas connecting those distributions to scattering observables. Finally, we connect this framework to polarized $^{7}$Li through its collinear limits and nuclear spin-orbital correlations.

papers.title: Kernel moments and thermodynamic stability in nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio models
papers.summary: We study thermodynamic consistency and stability in a covariant two-flavor nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model at zero chemical potential in the homogeneous quark mean-field approximation. A controlled large-source expansion gives a sufficient entropy-sign criterion directly from Euclidean kernel moments, without locating propagator poles. At fixed couplings and kernel, every admissible positive Gaussian mixture develops negative total entropy at sufficiently large source mass for each fixed positive temperature. In a separate light-source fit to pion observables and a subtracted condensate, one quartic-exponent kernel has positive entropy and heat capacity for all $T>0$, while $dP/dε=s/C_V$ exceeds unity on a finite interval. This constructive example separates thermal positivity from the static EOS slope test. Numerical refits show that the enhancement weakens with the condensate input, and a certified counterexample excludes uniform thermal positivity over the adopted matching domain. The results provide diagnostics of the mean-field functional, rather than a preferred phenomenological kernel. Omitted thermal mesons can change the low-temperature slope test, and the static derivative does not determine a real-time front velocity.

papers.title: Rethinking World Models for Biosignals
papers.summary: World models promise to learn how systems evolve and respond to actions, enabling simulation, planning and decision-making. Bringing this promise to biosignals requires more than accurate prediction of physiological recordings. We examine existing biosignal world models through two requirements for intervention use: a genuine action and evidence of its causal effect. We identify three fundamental bottlenecks rooted in physiology: Temporal Latency, the variable delay between an action and its observable effect; System Openness, the influence of drivers beyond the modelled intervention; and Endogenous Dynamics, the system's ongoing evolution without that intervention. Drawing on published evidence, we outline corresponding research directions and propose an Intervention-Effect Validation Checklist to guide evaluation. The aim is to help the biosignal community realise the core promise of world models by learning the latent mechanisms that govern physiological evolution and responses to interventions.

papers.title: Collective Benefits and Efficiency in Coupled Echo State Networks
papers.summary: Simple aggregation of independent responses ("wisdom of crowds") generally improves collective performance through statistical facilitation, but interaction among members can sometimes hinder group outcomes. However, under certain circumstances, coordination studies show that interacting groups can outperform their individual members and nominal groups, and interaction can also be more efficient than independence. We present a reservoir computing model to investigate how interaction can enhance joint performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Echo state networks were trained independently to identify Japanese speakers from vowel recordings and tested jointly with and without coupled feedback. Model pairs reproduced the dyadic advantage reported by Bahrami et al. (2010) with interaction via pooled-feedback, but not when independent responses were aggregated together. Model dynamics revealed that interaction was beneficial whereas aggregated outputs were prone to diverging from runaway feedback over time. In terms of efficiency, larger groups of smaller interacting models outperformed smaller groups of larger models while equating for total amount of group computation. Our results offer a formal framework for explaining when and why interaction enhances collective intelligence.
papers.comment: Experiment one presented at the 48th Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society as a full paper talk in "Collective Intelligence."

papers.title: Parton and nuclear dynamics at large $x$: the CJ26 global QCD analysis
papers.summary: We present the new CTEQ-JLab global QCD analysis, called CJ26, that simultaneously fits parton distribution functions of the proton and nuclear effects in deuteron targets. This work includes, for the first time in a global fit, the full set of JLab 6 GeV inclusive DIS measurements and the first published JLab 12 GeV data. The analysis focuses on the large-$x$ region, and carefully treats the interplay between higher-twist effects and off-shell corrections in low-energy proton and deuteron target data. We discuss their effect on quark and gluon distributions, and highlight the importance of quantifying the experimental correlated systematic uncertainty to achieve fits of the highest accuracy. We also outline how upcoming data may help unravel the nuclear and partonic dynamics in light nuclei. The extracted next-to-leading order parton distributions are available on the CJ web pages in LHAPDF format for general use, accompanied by leading- and higher-twist structure functions calculated with the simultaneously fitted PDFs, higher-twist corrections, and off-shell corrections. This write up clarifies several points that became clearer while finalizing the CJ26 paper and can be read as a companion to the latter.
papers.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. Proceedings of DIS2026, Bologna, Italy, 4-8 May 2026

papers.title: Designing Independent Variation: A Guided Iteration Methodology for Price Experiments in Short, Correlated Panels
papers.summary: Estimation error in short, correlated pricing panels is dominated by trajectory dispersion rather than sampling noise, creating an identification shortfall that only independently assigned variation can resolve. We propose a guided iteration methodology to decide how much variation to generate, where, and for how long: a cyclic price-perturbation scheme under a revenue-at-risk budget, framed as variance minimization over design-specific error covariances, analogous to portfolio selection. We establish four key results: (1) a closed-form minimum-variance combination rule; (2) proof that a convex cost of intensity yields an interior, spread-out allocation, whereas under a concave tolerable-volume-loss cost, concentrating intensity into fewer perturbations pays off only with heterogeneous candidates, priced-in fixed costs, or perturbations beyond the cost curve's inflection point; (3) a discounted recursion yielding a data-dependent exit timeline from the experimentation zone; and (4) an application to Dominick's retail data, in which about five designed independent units match the precision of approximately 700 passive equivalents in the anchor category, while a fast proxy across ten categories achieves a median 97% variance reduction relative to passive panels. Sixteen comparisons (eleven pre-specified) support the theory: greedy selection achieves 90-93% of the global optimum across more than fifty exhaustively verifiable instances, and the recursion reaches its predicted 90%-of-steady-state benchmark two cycles early, though a parametric bootstrap indicates that its delta-method interval understates the right-tail risk. Boundary conditions show that regularized covariance estimators extend plug-in noise tolerance from 29% to beyond 50%, submodularity holds up to a clear curvature threshold, and a shared shock imposes a fundamental precision floor.

papers.title: Continuity of stable marriage correspondences
papers.summary: We study a continuum version of the stable marriage problem, in which each agent has a variable mass to be paired to the opposite side. An agent's mass is interpretable as the divisible time of a single atomistic agent, or as a mass of infinitesimal agents of a particular type. Our object of interest is the mapping between the vector of masses to the set of stable matches. As in the canonical stable marriage model, the set of stable matches can be multi-valued, so this mapping is a correspondence. This correspondence is continuous if and only if the stable match is unique, implying that small changes in the masses may cause discontinuous jumps in the set of stable matches.

papers.title: Unit-Demand Pricing for Min-Buying Customers
papers.summary: We study the unit-demand pricing problem under \textit{min-buying} behavior, where customers purchase the lowest-priced item that yields non-negative utility. In contrast to the quasi-linear model, we show that uniform pricing becomes substantially more effective under min-buying. First, we study symmetric environments. We show that for min-buying customers with independent and identically distributed valuations, a uniform price across items is optimal. We then extend this optimality result to all valuations drawn from exchangeable and affiliated distributions. However, uniform pricing is not optimal in all symmetric environments: for min-buying customers we construct an exchangeable and non-affiliated valuation distribution for which the gap between uniform pricing and optimal item pricing is logarithmic in the number of items. This gap is tight and matches the worst-case gap in the quasi-linear setting. Next, we consider asymmetric environments in which valuations are independent but not identically distributed. When these valuations are regular and customers are min-buying, we show that a uniform price guarantees approximately 69.86\% of the optimal item-pricing revenue and this is tight. Overall, our results highlight that the value of non-uniform pricing substantially diminishes, and often disappears entirely, under more conservative demand models in which customers engage in satisficing behaviors such as min-buying.

papers.title: Internal Nucleon Properties and the Equation of State of Ultra-Dense Matter
papers.summary: The question of the link between the nucleon properties and the equation of state of ultra-dense matter, both being composed of quarks and gluons, is investigated by adopting a soliton model to describe internal nucleon properties and a direct mapping between nucleon and quark matter to obtain the equation of state of ultra-dense matter. We compare $π+ω$ and $π+ω+ρ$ soliton models and analyze the presence of a pressure singularity at the nucleon center due to the $ρ$ field. This singularity impacts the equation of state in ultra-dense matter. Only the pressure derived from the canonical energy-momentum tensor has a singularity, while the Belinfante pseudo-gauge transformation of the energy-momentum tensor generates an internal pressure without a singularity. We then investigate predictions for the equation of state of ultra-dense matter based on different prescriptions for the nucleon pressure. It is shown that none of the prescriptions agree with the thermodynamical pressure defined in uniform matter. The mismatch between any equation of state and the thermodynamical one questions the simplicity of the direct mapping between finite-size nucleon properties and uniform matter as well as the role of the nucleon surface in the internal energy density and the pressure.

papers.title: FINESSE: A Versatile Beamline for Fundamental Interactions with Neutrons at the European Spallation SourcE
papers.summary: FINESSE (A Versatile Beamline for \textbf{F}undamental \textbf{I}nteractions with \textbf{N}eutrons at the \textbf{E}uropean \textbf{S}pallation \textbf{S}ourc\textbf{E}) is a proposed versatile beamline for fundamental interactions with neutrons at the European Spallation Source. Building on the HIBEAM design studies, FINESSE extends the original concept into a dual-guide beamline capable of operating either in a high-flux configuration or in a low-background configuration within a single ESS beam port. The high-flux branch is optimized for rare-process searches, including neutron--antineutron oscillations, neutron--sterile-neutron transitions, axion-like-particle searches, neutron charge measurements, and rare neutron decays. The low-background branch is designed for precision measurements requiring strong suppression of prompt and line-of-sight backgrounds, with a cryogenic neutron electric-dipole-moment experiment used as a benchmark case. A baseline exchangeable-guide concept has been developed in which only short guide sections inside the ESS bunker are exchanged, while the upstream extraction system and chopper positions remain fixed. A staged implementation, Short FINESSE, would use the upstream section of the high-flux beamline together with a compact magnetically controlled experimental region, enabling an early physics and R\&D programme before completion of the full facility. This paper summarizes the scientific case, beamline concept, guide simulations, chopper and timing system, magnetic-field control, detector developments, and staged implementation strategy. FINESSE would establish a long-term particle-physics infrastructure at ESS, providing a beamline for both discovery-driven searches and precision neutron measurements throughout the lifetime of the facility.

papers.title: Creative destruction: Human-AI competition in an experimental market
papers.summary: We study two hypotheses for how a human role in production could persist despite growing AI capabilities. Humans might have a durable advantage in taste, designing better products even as AI agents automate routine tasks, or consumers might intrinsically prefer that humans have a hand in production. In our experiment, participants act as producers, designing computer games with an AI coding agent, and as consumers who buy them. Across three studies (N = 1,025), we find no evidence for either hypothesis. Games designed by an AI on its own outperform those of human producers, including both amateurs and professional creatives. Human producers do not anticipate the AI's advantage. Revealing whether a game is human-designed does not raise consumers' willingness to pay for the product.

papers.title: Beyond Successful Play: Diagnosing Opponent Modeling in Large Language Models
papers.summary: Language-model agents are expected to adapt to others whose behavior changes through interaction. Yet adaptation may rely on learned behavioral patterns rather than theory of mind (ToM): the ability to infer others' mental states, including beliefs and intentions. We introduce a benchmark and diagnostic framework for repeated hide-and-seek against algorithmic opponents with explicitly defined recursive belief updates. Their ground-truth beliefs and action probabilities let us distinguish adaptive play, action prediction, and belief tracking through live interaction, fixed-history evaluation, and controlled information interventions. With structured elicitation and behavioral supervised fine-tuning (SFT), we find improved play in several tested settings, but diagnostics reveal limitations in opponent prediction and belief tracking. We test whether supervising opponent action probabilities can address this predictive deficit in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Predictions improve when the model is told the opponent's type and parameter settings, but become less accurate when it must infer the opponent from history without this information. Training on examples that also omit these details reduces the gap, although improvements vary across opponents. Is this limitation specific to smaller open-weight models, or does it also appear in a frontier model? GPT-5.4 also benefits from correct opponent beliefs: supplying them improves its predictions and choices, whereas deeper explicit belief reports and self-generated memory do not consistently improve forecasting from interaction history. This contrast suggests that using useful belief information is easier than inferring it autonomously, even for a frontier model. Together, our findings distinguish improved play and action prediction from reliable belief tracking, providing a framework for evaluating mentalizing and testing targeted improvements.

papers.title: Lepton Flavour Universality in Semileptonic $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$ Transitions
papers.summary: Using continuum Schwinger function methods, we deliver parameter-free pointwise predictions for the complete set of twelve Standard Model (SM) $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$, i.e., $b\to c$, semileptonic transition form factors on the entire kinematically accessible domain. Therewith, we calculate SM theory values for the decay-rate ratios of $τ$ and $μ$ final states: $\{ R(D) \, , \, R(D)^\ast \} = \{ 0.290(11) \, , \, 0.267(5) \}$, $\{ R(D_{s}) \, , \, R(D_{s}^{\ast}) \} = \{ 0.283(11) \, , \, 0.251(5) \}$. The former is consistent with an existing average of SM estimates, but disagrees with the experimental average by $2.8σ$. Comparing transitions with light quark and strange quark spectators, we find a $2.3σ$ signal for violation of SU$(3)$ flavour symmetry, expressed at the 5% level in $D_{(s)}^\ast$ final states. It is induced by Higgs boson couplings into the strong interaction and modulated by phenomena deriving from emergent features of the strong interaction.
